help.bannerDesc: Parameter reference, scene presets, strategy evidence and hardware speed. The "?" next to each parameter in the interface opens its entry here.
help.benchTitle: Training speed: WildCat and Nuke 17.0v2 CopyCat on the same machine
help.benchSetup: Same workstation, same GPU; 40 frames of 772×855 half-float EXR, Multi-Resolution on, Mixed Precision Adaptive. Values are the steady training speed of each resolution stage (steps/s, higher is faster).
help.benchLoadFailed: Speed data could not be loaded
help.benchNote1: The 1/4 and 1/2 stages gain most: each training step is recorded as one CUDA Graph, which removes the fixed scheduling cost of every step.
help.benchNote2: The full-resolution 1/1 stage is limited mainly by GPU compute and gains less than the first two stages.
help.benchNote3: A dataset smaller than 60% of the free GPU memory stays resident on the GPU; larger datasets are prefetched from pinned memory. On machines with two GPUs, the full-frame preview and validation run on the secondary GPU.
help.gpuSpeedDbTitle: GPU speed table (used for training time estimates)
help.gpuSpeedDbDesc: Training speed of the measured GPUs in each resolution stage. The estimated duration of a new task is computed from this table and corrected with the measured speed once training runs.
help.gpuSpeedUntestedNote: GPUs not in the table are estimated from the measured ones by memory bandwidth and clock; once training runs, the remaining time is corrected with the measured speed.
help.valKfCommon: On · threshold {threshold} · {span} keyframes on each side
help.evIntro: This page gives the test method and the test results behind the advanced settings and the scene presets. For everyday work, Parameter Reference and Scene Presets are sufficient.

admin.gpuNeedTwoEnabledTip: A secondary GPU requires at least 2 enabled GPUs.
admin.gpuDrainingNote: Takes no new tasks after the current one
admin.storageCardDesc: Uploaded datasets (users/), training results (run/), task configurations (config/) and the preview cache (cache/) can be moved to a large volume. The analytics database stays in the program folder. Changes take effect immediately, without a restart.
admin.storageRootPlaceholder: Leave empty for the default directory ({defaultPath}), or enter a path on a large volume, e.g. /mnt/raid_nvme/wildcat_data

lab.comboReason_cg_1: Recommended, same as the Clean-up preset: Medium, 1 px crop grid, gradient term 0.05, averaged weights (EMA).
lab.comboReason_cg_2: Gradient term off (1 px crop grid and averaged weights kept), everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_cg_3: Model Size Small, everything else as recommended; about 2/3 of the training time.
lab.comboReason_cg_6: Crop Size raised to 384 (256 when the short side of the plate is below 720 px), everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_cg_7: All three composite-loss terms (Charbonnier 0.25, gradient term 0.05, highlight damping 0.5) plus horizontal flip 50 %, without averaged weights.
lab.comboReason_kd_1: Recommended, same as the Keying preset: Small, 1 px crop grid, gradient term 0.15, averaged weights (EMA).
lab.comboReason_kd_2: Gradient term off (1 px crop grid and averaged weights kept), everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_kd_3: Gradient term 0.05, everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_kd_4: Model Size Medium, everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_kd_5: Gradient term 0.30, everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_kd_6: Crop Size raised to 384 (256 when the short side of the plate is below 720 px), everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_kd_7: All three composite-loss terms (Charbonnier 0.30, gradient term 0.15, highlight damping 0.35), without averaged weights.
lab.comboReason_bf_1: Recommended, same as the Defocus preset: Large, 1 px crop grid, composite loss (Charbonnier 0.25, gradient term 0.10, highlight damping 0.5), stage ratios 15/25/60.
lab.comboReason_bf_2: Composite loss off, everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_bf_3: Medium, 1 px crop grid, stage ratios 15/25/60, no composite loss; trains faster than Large.
lab.comboReason_bf_4: Large, 1 px crop grid, equal stages (Nuke CopyCat default), no composite loss.
lab.comboReason_bf_5: Small, 1 px crop grid, stage ratios 15/25/60, no composite loss.
lab.comboReason_bf_6: Large, 1 px crop grid, stage ratios 15/25/60, Crop Size 384 (256 when the short side of the plate is below 720 px), no composite loss.
lab.comboReason_dg_1: Recommended, same as the Degrain preset: Small, 1 px crop grid.
lab.comboReason_dg_2: Plus gradient term 0.05, everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_dg_3: Model Size Medium, everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_dg_4: All three composite-loss terms (Charbonnier 0.25, gradient term 0.05, highlight damping 0.5), everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_dg_5: Crop Size raised to 384 (256 when the short side of the plate is below 720 px), everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_dg_6: Plus gradient term 0.15, everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_rm_1: Recommended, same as the Roto preset: Small, 1 px crop grid. Roto results depend mostly on the number and spacing of keyframes.
lab.comboReason_rm_2: Plus Charbonnier 0.25 and gradient term 0.05, everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_rm_3: Crop Size raised to 384 (256 when the short side of the plate is below 720 px), everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_rm_4: Plus gradient term 0.05, everything else as recommended.

lab.comboReason_fe_2: Comparison: keyframe commonality off, everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_fe_3: Crop grid kept at 4 px (Nuke CopyCat default), everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_fe_nokf: Recommended configuration without keyframe commonality: Medium, 1 px crop grid, Charbonnier 0.25, averaged weights (EMA). Keyframe commonality cannot be used on this dataset; the reason is shown above.
lab.comboReason_nuke: Nuke CopyCat defaults: 4 px crop grid, plain MSE, no advanced settings, no early stop. Same Model Size as the recommended configuration.
lab.formPatienceClearTip: The form carries Stop after best score. Click to clear it and train to the full Epochs.
lab.comboReason_fe_4: Model Size Small, everything else as recommended; about 2/3 of the training time.
lab.comboReason_fe_5: Keyframe commonality without the overall look, everything else as recommended. For shots whose keyframes differ in overall density or colour on purpose, such as a wound that darkens over time or make-up that appears gradually.
lab.comboReason_fe_6: Keyframe commonality with RAFT optical flow, everything else as recommended. Aligns keyframes more accurately on fast motion; the preparation before training takes longer.
lab.comboReason_fe_7: Model Size Small, everything else as the first task; about 2/3 of its training time.
lab.comboReason_fe_8: Comparison: without Charbonnier (pixel loss MSE only, as in Nuke), everything else as recommended.
lab.comboReason_fe_9: Without Charbonnier (pixel loss MSE only), everything else as the first task.
lab.comboReason_cg_kf: Recommended plus keyframe commonality. For shots whose hand-painted keyframes do not fully agree with each other.
lab.comboReason_cg_8: Recommended plus Charbonnier 0.25. Does not raise PSNR, but on grainy live-action plates it changes fewer pixels of the unedited area.
lab.comboReason_dg_7: Epochs 100000, everything else as recommended. Degrain shots usually stop improving beyond about 100000 Epochs.

task_name.title: Task Name
task_name.summary: Name of the training task and of its folder: model files, checkpoints and previews are saved under run/task name/.
task_name.body:
## What it does
Identifies the task in the task list, the queue and the downloaded files. Spaces and special characters are replaced with underscores; letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.` are kept.

## Recommended values
Use a separate name for each shot and each attempt. While a task is training or queued, no other task can be submitted under the same name.

dataset.title: Dataset
dataset.summary: The dataset to train on: keyframe pairs (Input and Ground Truth), optionally with the shot's validation sequence.
dataset.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
The image pairs connected to the Input and Ground Truth inputs of the CopyCat node.

## What it does
Click the field to open the dataset list. The selected dataset is previewed below: Input on the left, Ground Truth on the right; when the dataset has a validation sequence, the preview can switch to the whole sequence. The dataset's channels decide which [[doc:channels]] options are available, and the number of keyframes enters the total step count (see [[doc:epochs]]).

## Requirements
Datasets are created on the Datasets page, see [[doc:dataset_keyframes]]. The validation sequence is optional (see [[doc:dataset_validation_sequence]]); auto-extend, the checkpoint recommendation, keyframe commonality and the training-quality measures need it.

device.title: Use Device
device.summary: The GPU the task trains on. Auto Queue picks a free GPU; when all GPUs are busy, the task waits in the queue.
device.body:
## What it does
- **Auto Queue** (default): starts at once on a free GPU, the primary GPU first; when all GPUs are busy, the task waits in the queue and runs on the first GPU that becomes free.
- **A specific GPU**: trains only on that GPU; while it is busy, the task waits for it.

Each GPU trains one task at a time. The options show the state of each GPU and when it is expected to be free; disabled GPUs cannot be selected.

## Limitations
Tasks of temporary users always use Auto Queue.

init_weights.title: Initial Weights
init_weights.summary: Where training starts: from scratch or from a saved checkpoint. With existing weights, Model Size and Channels follow those weights and are locked.
init_weights.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
**Initial Weights** of the CopyCat node.

## What it does
- **None** (default): starts from randomly initialised weights; Model Size and Channels can be chosen freely.
- **Checkpoint**: continues from a saved checkpoint. Model Size and Channels follow the checkpoint and cannot be changed; "Use the checkpoint's training dataset" selects the dataset the checkpoint was trained on.

## When to use
Use Checkpoint to build on earlier training, for example after keyframes were added or changed. To continue the same task, extend its Epochs on the task page (see [[doc:monitor_extend]]).

model_size.title: Model Size
model_size.summary: Network capacity: Small, Medium (default) or Large. Larger models take longer per step. Same as Model Size in Nuke CopyCat.
model_size.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
**Model Size** of the CopyCat node, default Medium. The three networks have the same structure as in CopyCat; the trained model works directly in Nuke's Inference node.

## What it does
| Model Size | Parameters |
|---|---|
| Small | about 1.0 M |
| Medium | about 2.6 M |
| Large | about 6.9 M |

Larger models take longer per step; a Large step takes several times as long as a Small one.

## Recommended values
A larger model is not always better: defocus shots do better with Large; clean-up and face shots do better with Medium than with Small; keying is the same with Small and Medium; degrain and roto shots do better with Small. The scene presets choose the Model Size for their task type.

## Limitations
When Initial Weights uses a checkpoint, Model Size follows the checkpoint and is locked.

epochs.title: Epochs
epochs.summary: Number of passes over all keyframes; sets the total number of training steps. Same as Epochs in Nuke CopyCat.
epochs.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
**Epochs** of the CopyCat node, default 10000.

## What it does
Total Steps = ⌈Epochs × number of keyframes ÷ Batch Size⌉, shown to the right of the field. For example, 8 keyframes, Batch Size 8 and 10000 Epochs give 10000 steps.

## Recommended values
Start with the default. Once the Loss curve and the preview on the task page stop changing, further training adds little; a finished task can be continued by extending its Epochs on the task page (see [[doc:monitor_extend]]).

## Limitations
Scene presets never change Epochs. Temporary users may have an Epochs limit, shown next to the field.

auto_extend.title: Auto-extend
auto_extend.summary: After the set Epochs, keeps training in further rounds while the fit to the training keyframes still improves clearly, up to a limit. Off by default.
auto_extend.body:
## What it does
When the set Epochs are reached, the saved checkpoints are evaluated on the validation sequence; if the fit to the training keyframes (PSNR) is still improving (by at least 0.20 dB per extension round), training continues for about 30% of the Epochs and the check is repeated. At most 4 rounds; the total never exceeds 2.5 times the set Epochs or the account's Epochs limit. Auto-extend never ends training early.

## When to use
When the set Epochs may be too few and training should top up on its own. The criterion looks only at the training keyframes and cannot tell whether the in-between frames benefit as well; degrain shots do not improve with longer training, so leave it off for them.

## Requirements
The dataset has a validation sequence (see [[doc:dataset_validation_sequence]]).

## Limitations
When off (default), the task trains exactly the set Epochs, as Nuke CopyCat does. The number of extension rounds is shown with the checkpoint recommendation on the task page.

batch_size.title: Batch Size
batch_size.summary: Number of crops trained together in each step. Auto uses 8 and halves it when GPU memory is short. Same as Batch Size in Nuke CopyCat.
batch_size.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
**Batch Size** of the CopyCat node (Auto / Manual); Auto is 8.

## What it does
- **Auto** (default): 8, halved step by step when it does not fit in GPU memory.
- **Manual**: any positive integer.

Batch Size never exceeds the number of keyframes: with fewer keyframes, the batch equals the keyframe count and the actual value is shown next to the field (Nuke CopyCat does not start training in that case). Batch Size enters the total step count, see [[doc:epochs]].

## Recommended values
Auto.

crop_size.title: Crop Size
crop_size.summary: Side length, in pixels, of the square crops taken from random positions of the keyframes during training; default 256. Same as Crop Size in Nuke CopyCat.
crop_size.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
**Crop Size** of the CopyCat node, default 256.

## What it does
Each step trains on Crop Size × Crop Size pixel crops taken from random positions of the keyframes. With Multi-Resolution on, the three resolution stages use Crop/4, Crop/2 and Crop (at least 32 px, rounded down to a multiple of 16 px and never larger than the short side of the frame at that stage); the actual sizes are shown to the right of the field. Options: 32, 64, 128, 256, 384, 512.

## Recommended values
256. Crop Size should stay well below the frame height so that the crop positions vary enough. Larger crops take considerably more time and GPU memory per step.

## Limitations
Scene presets use 256, reduced automatically for small frames.

multi_resolution.title: Multi-Resolution
multi_resolution.summary: Trains first on frames scaled to 1/4 and 1/2, then at full resolution, each stage taking a third of the steps. On by default, as in Nuke CopyCat.
multi_resolution.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
**Use Multi-Resolution Training** of the CopyCat node.

## What it does
Training runs in three resolution stages, 1/4 → 1/2 → 1/1, with the steps split into thirds; frames are scaled down with Bicubic filtering and the crop shrinks accordingly (see [[doc:crop_size]]). Steps at low resolution are faster, so the whole run takes clearly less time. With Off, the whole run trains at full resolution.

## Limitations
The stage ratios among the advanced settings (see [[doc:adv_stages]]) are available only when this is on.

mixed_precision.title: Mixed Precision
mixed_precision.summary: Whether training computes in FP16 or FP32. Adaptive (default) picks the faster one for each resolution stage.
mixed_precision.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
The hidden knob **useAutomaticMixedPrecision** of CopyCat, not shown in the Nuke interface.

## What it does
- **Adaptive** (default): before each resolution stage, FP16 mixed precision and FP32 are both tried on a separate copy of the model and the faster one is used; the trial does not affect the trained weights.
- **Disabled**: FP32 throughout.
- **Force Enabled**: FP16 mixed precision throughout.

Mixed precision applies to the computation only; the model weights are always stored and updated in FP32.

## Recommended values
Adaptive.

channels.title: Channels
channels.summary: The model's input and output channels, for example RGB → RGB, RGB → RGBA or RGB → Alpha. Must match the dataset's channels.
channels.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
Set automatically by CopyCat from the channels connected to Input and Ground Truth.

## What it does
| Option | Typical use |
|---|---|
| RGB → RGB (3→3) | Colour changes: clean-up, degrain, defocus, face edits |
| RGB → RGBA (3→4) | Colour and alpha together, for example keying with despill |
| RGBA → RGBA (4→4) | Alpha on both input and output |
| RGB → Alpha (3→1) | Matte only, for example roto |
| RGBA → Alpha (4→1) | Input with alpha, matte only |

Options that need more channels than the dataset contains are disabled and show the dataset's channel counts.

## Limitations
When Initial Weights uses a checkpoint, Channels follow the checkpoint and are locked.

checkpoint_interval.title: Checkpoint Interval
checkpoint_interval.summary: How often, in steps, a model is saved; default 1000. Same as Checkpoint Interval in Nuke CopyCat.
checkpoint_interval.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
**Checkpoint Interval** of the CopyCat node, default 1000.

## What it does
At every interval, a model file (format: see [[doc:model_files]]) and a checkpoint for continued training are saved in the task folder; they are also saved when training is paused or finishes. All saved versions are listed in the model versions table on the task page (see [[doc:monitor_models]]) and can be downloaded one by one.

## Recommended values
1000. A smaller interval gives more model versions to choose from and uses more disk space. Minimum 10 steps.

contact_sheet_interval.title: Contact Sheet Interval
contact_sheet_interval.summary: How often, in steps, a contact sheet is saved and the full-frame preview on the task page is refreshed; default 100. Same as Contact Sheet Interval in Nuke CopyCat.
contact_sheet_interval.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
**Contact Sheet Interval** of the CopyCat node, default 100.

## What it does
At every interval, a contact sheet `Training_YYMMDD_HHMMSS.<step>.png` is saved: 3 rows for 3 training crops, 3 columns for input, Ground Truth and the current output (see [[doc:monitor_contact_sheet]]); the full-frame preview on the task page is refreshed at the same time (see [[doc:monitor_preview]]).

## Limitations
With [[doc:preview_gpu]] set to off, no contact sheets or full-frame previews are made and this field cannot be edited.

learning_rate.title: Learning Rate
learning_rate.summary: Initial learning rate of the Adam optimiser, default 0.0001, decaying to 0 over the run. Corresponds to the hidden learningRate knob of Nuke CopyCat.
learning_rate.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
The hidden knob **learningRate** of CopyCat, default 0.0001, not shown in the Nuke interface.

## What it does
The learning rate starts at the set value and falls to 0 at the last step along a polynomial curve (power 0.3); training uses the Adam optimiser, as CopyCat does.

## Recommended values
0.0001 (default). Too high a value can make training unstable, too low a value slows convergence.

seed.title: Seed
seed.summary: Random seed for the initial weights, the order in which keyframes are drawn and the crop positions; default 0. Corresponds to the hidden seed knob of Nuke CopyCat.
seed.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
The hidden knob **seed** of CopyCat, default 0, not shown in the Nuke interface.

## What it does
With the same data, settings and Seed, training uses the same random sequence (GPU computation can still cause tiny numerical differences). A different Seed gives a slightly different result.

## Recommended values
0 (default). Use the same Seed when comparing two sets of settings.

log_interval.title: Log Interval
log_interval.summary: How often, in steps, the Loss is recorded; default 10. Fixed at 10 inside Nuke CopyCat.
log_interval.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
CopyCat records every 10 steps; this cannot be changed there.

## What it does
Sets how densely the Loss curve on the task page is sampled and how often the training log and the `.summary` file are written. It does not affect the training result.

## Recommended values
10 (default).

color_pipeline.title: Colour space (ACEScg / sRGB)
color_pipeline.summary: Training data is stored and trained as linear EXR (ACEScg by default); previews in the browser are converted to sRGB with OCIO.
color_pipeline.body:
## What it does
- **Data**: datasets are stored as linear EXR, ACEScg by default; uploads are converted according to the dataset's input colour space (see [[doc:dataset_input_colorspace]]). Training and the exported model work on linear values, as in Nuke CopyCat.
- **Preview**: images on the task page and the Datasets page are converted to sRGB with OCIO for display only; training is not affected.

## Requirements
When the model is used in Nuke, the images fed to the Inference node should be in the same linear colour space as the training data.

model_files.title: Model files
model_files.summary: Each checkpoint saves a TorchScript model file (.pt, named as in CopyCat); in Nuke, CatFileCreator converts it to a .cat file for the Inference node.
model_files.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
CopyCat saves `Training_YYMMDD_HHMMSS.<step>.cat` in its training directory.

## What it does
The model file `Training_YYMMDD_HHMMSS.<step>.pt` is saved in the task folder `run/<task name>/`, where `<step>` is the step at which it was saved; the naming follows CopyCat. The model versions table on the task page lists all versions for download, one by one or as a package.

## Requirements
In Nuke, read the .pt file with a **CatFileCreator** node, set the input and output channels as in training, create the .cat file and load it into an **Inference** node.

speed_options.title: Speed options
speed_options.summary: Settings that change only how the computation is executed, not the training itself; all on by default.
speed_options.body:
## What it does
None of these options changes the mathematics of training: with the same data, settings and Seed, training runs the same as with them off (floating-point operations may run in a different order, which causes tiny numerical differences), and it follows the way Nuke CopyCat trains. The master switch turns all of them on or off ([[doc:preview_gpu]] excepted). With all of them off, training runs the way CopyCat executes it, reading the data from system memory at every step, and is clearly slower.

## Recommended values
All on.

speed_gpu_resident.title: Dataset resident in VRAM (gpu_resident)
speed_gpu_resident.summary: When GPU memory allows, keeps the whole dataset in GPU memory so that no data has to be loaded during the steps.
speed_gpu_resident.body:
## What it does
At the start of each resolution stage the free GPU memory is checked: if the stage's data fits, it is kept in GPU memory as a whole (half-float EXR losslessly as FP16); otherwise the data is prefetched from system memory, which is slightly slower. To leave room for training itself, the data takes at most 60% of the free GPU memory.

speed_cuda_graph.title: Full-step CUDA Graph (cuda_graph)
speed_cuda_graph.summary: Records one training step (forward, backward, loss scaling and parameter update) as a CUDA Graph and replays it, cutting the scheduling overhead of every step.
speed_cuda_graph.body:
## What it does
Each step runs on the GPU with a single launch; the gain is largest in the low-resolution stages.

## Requirements
Needs [[doc:speed_fused_adam]] to be on.

speed_fused_adam.title: Fused Adam (fused_adam)
speed_fused_adam.summary: Performs the Adam parameter update in one fused CUDA kernel; formula and settings are unchanged.
speed_fused_adam.body:
## What it does
Same formula and settings as standard Adam; the updates of all parameters are merged into one kernel call. [[doc:speed_cuda_graph]] needs this option.

speed_channels_last.title: NHWC memory layout (channels_last)
speed_channels_last.summary: Stores image data in NHWC order (channels last), which suits GPUs with Tensor Cores; the values are unchanged.
speed_channels_last.body:
## What it does
Changes only the order in which data is laid out in GPU memory; convolutions run faster on GPUs with Tensor Cores.

speed_cudnn_benchmark.title: cuDNN auto-tuning (cudnn_benchmark)
speed_cudnn_benchmark.summary: At the start of each resolution stage, tests the convolution algorithms for the fixed input size and uses the fastest.
speed_cudnn_benchmark.body:
## What it does
Each stage starts with a few seconds of testing; every step after that is faster.

speed_async_io.title: Asynchronous saving (async_io)
speed_async_io.summary: Writes checkpoints, exports models and encodes preview images in the background without interrupting training.
speed_async_io.body:
## What it does
Saving and exporting run in a background thread, so training does not wait for disk writes.

preview_gpu.title: Preview / validation GPU (preview_gpu)
preview_gpu.summary: Where the full-frame preview and the keyframe validation are computed: auto uses a second GPU, same uses the training GPU, off turns the preview off.
preview_gpu.body:
## What it does
- **auto** (default): with a second GPU, preview and validation run asynchronously on it and the training GPU only trains; with one GPU it behaves like same.
- **same**: runs asynchronously on the training GPU.
- **off**: no full-frame previews or contact sheets; the keyframe validation is not affected.

Preview and validation compute in FP32, the default of Nuke's Inference node.

eta_estimate.title: Estimated training time
eta_estimate.summary: Training time estimated from the measured speed of the GPU, not counting time spent waiting in the queue.
eta_estimate.body:
## What it does
Calculated from Model Size, Batch Size, Crop Size, the resolution stages and the advanced settings that are on, using the GPU speed database. For a GPU model in the database its measured speed is used; otherwise the estimate is based on similar GPUs. Once training runs, the remaining time on the task page follows the actual speed.

adv_overview.title: Advanced settings
adv_overview.summary: Six optional modules, all off by default. With all of them off, training is identical to Nuke CopyCat; none of them changes the network, so exported models still work in Nuke Inference.
adv_overview.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat

CopyCat has no such settings. With all modules off, crop sampling, loss, learning rate, resolution stages and the exported model are the same as in CopyCat.

## What it does

Each module changes one part of training:

- [[doc:adv_crop_grid]]: where full-resolution crops start
- [[doc:adv_loss]]: the loss function used for training
- [[doc:adv_stages]]: the share of steps in each Multi-Resolution stage
- [[doc:adv_ema]]: which weights previews, checkpoints and exports use
- [[doc:adv_augment]]: flips and exposure changes of the training crops
- [[doc:adv_kf_common]]: a consistency pass over the keyframes before training

## When to use

When unsure, leave all modules off or use the [[doc:presets_overview|scene preset]] for the type of shot. "Reset to Nuke defaults" switches every module off.

## Limitations

All modules act on training only and never change the network; a trained model is used in Nuke exactly like one trained by CopyCat. The counter next to the panel title shows how many modules are in effect.

adv_crop_grid.title: Crop grid
adv_crop_grid.summary: Changes the step of full-resolution crop origins from 4 px to 1 px so that training covers every sampling phase of full-frame inference. No extra training time.
adv_crop_grid.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat

CopyCat places full-resolution crops on a 4 px grid measured from the bottom edge of the frame (Nuke's origin is at the bottom left). The network downsamples twice by 2, and full-frame inference (Inference) samples on a grid measured from the top edge. When the plate height is not a multiple of 4 (for example 2048×858), training and inference sample at different phases, and at inference the model works at a phase it never saw in training.

## What it does

A 1 px step covers all 16 sampling phases (4 horizontal × 4 vertical), so inference always runs at a phase seen in training, and the crops come from more positions. To remove only the phase offset, keep the 4 px step and set the [[doc:adv_crop_grid_anchor|grid anchor]] to the top edge.

## When to use

Suits most tasks; every scene preset except Nuke defaults uses 1 px. The effect is largest on clean-up shots and grows with training length; on roto shots it makes little difference.

## Recommended values

[[doc:adv_crop_grid_step|Grid step]] 1 px.

## Limitations

Changes only where full-resolution crops start; training speed, the network and the exported model stay the same.

adv_crop_grid_step.title: Grid step
adv_crop_grid_step.summary: Spacing of full-resolution crop origins: 1 px (recommended) or 4 px (as in CopyCat). Lower-resolution stages scale it down.
adv_crop_grid_step.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat

Fixed at 4 px. With Multi-Resolution the 1/4, 1/2 and 1/1 stages use 1, 2 and 4 px.

## What it does

- **1 px**: 1 px in every stage; covers every sampling phase.
- **4 px**: as in CopyCat. The module only counts as on when the [[doc:adv_crop_grid_anchor|grid anchor]] is set to the top edge.
- **2 px**: shown only for configurations that already use it, so that they keep running as configured; use 1 px for new tasks.

## Recommended values

1 px.

adv_crop_grid_anchor.title: Grid anchor
adv_crop_grid_anchor.summary: The edge the 4 px grid is measured from: bottom (as in CopyCat) or top (matches full-frame inference). Not used with the 1 px grid.
adv_crop_grid_anchor.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat

Measured from the bottom edge.

## What it does

With the top edge, training crops use the same sampling grid as full-frame inference (Inference), so there is no phase offset even when the plate height is not a multiple of 4; the step stays 4 px. When the height is a multiple of 4, both anchors give the same result.

## When to use

Choose the top edge to keep CopyCat's 4 px step on a plate whose height is not a multiple of 4. Not available with the 1 px grid.

## Limitations

For a model already trained with the bottom anchor (including models trained in Nuke), remove (plate height mod 4) rows from the top of the frame in Nuke before the Inference node to line the phases up.

adv_loss.title: Composite loss (Charbonnier / gradient term / highlight damping)
adv_loss.summary: Adds three optional terms to CopyCat's MSE in linear space: Charbonnier, a gradient term and highlight damping. Each can be set to 0 on its own.
adv_loss.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat

CopyCat computes the mean squared pixel error (MSE) directly in the linear working space (ACEScg). The squared error reacts weakly to very small residuals and strongly to errors in highlights.

## What it does

The model's input and output stay linear ACEScg and connect to Inference in Nuke without any conversion. The three terms only change how the error is computed during training:

- [[doc:adv_loss_charbonnier|Charbonnier]]: replaces part of the squared error with a smooth absolute error, which is more sensitive to small deviations.
- [[doc:adv_loss_grad|Gradient term]]: compares neighbouring-pixel differences of output and target, which reinforces edges and fine lines.
- [[doc:adv_loss_hdr|Highlight damping]]: lowers the weight of errors in highlights by the target's luminance (RGB only).

## When to use

- Keying: gradient term 0.15.
- Clean-up: gradient term 0.05.
- Defocus recovery: Charbonnier 0.25, gradient term 0.10, highlight damping 0.5.

Leave it off for other tasks.

## Recommended values

Switched on by hand, only the gradient term is set: 0.15 for 4-channel output, otherwise 0.05; Charbonnier and highlight damping are 0.

## Limitations

The Loss on the task page and in the log is still CopyCat's MSE at the finest resolution, so it can be compared directly with tasks that do not use this module.

adv_loss_charbonnier.title: Charbonnier ratio
adv_loss_charbonnier.summary: Share of the Charbonnier term (smooth absolute error) in the loss, 0–1; 0 = squared error (MSE) only. The Face edit preset uses 0.25: fewer changes to the unedited area, more accurate unseen frames.
adv_loss_charbonnier.body:
## What it does

Pixel loss = (1 − ratio) × MSE + ratio × Charbonnier. Charbonnier is √(residual² + ε²): for small residuals it behaves like the absolute error and gives small deviations more weight than the squared error does. ε is set by the [[doc:adv_loss_eps|smoothing constant]].

## When to use

- Defocus recovery: 0.25 (the setting of the Defocus preset).
- Face edits: 0.25 (the setting of the Face edit preset). More accurate unseen frames and edited areas, fewer changes to the unedited area.
- Other grainy live-action plates: 0.25 changes the unedited area less; the overall accuracy (PSNR) does not necessarily improve.
- Other tasks: 0.

## Recommended values

0 (the default when the composite loss is switched on by hand). Range 0–1.

## Limitations

Lowers accuracy on keying and clean-up; not recommended there. When the keyframes differ strongly from one another (each painted differently), it no longer raises accuracy on face shots either.

adv_loss_grad.title: Gradient weight
adv_loss_grad.summary: Adds the L1 error of neighbouring-pixel differences (first-order gradient) between output and target to the loss, which reinforces edges and fine lines. 0.15 recommended for keying, 0.05 for clean-up.
adv_loss_grad.body:
## What it does

On the output of every resolution, the horizontal and vertical neighbour differences of (output − target) are averaged as absolute values, multiplied by this weight and added to the loss. With [[doc:adv_loss_hdr|highlight damping]] on, the gradient term is damped with the same luminance weights.

## When to use

- Keying (RGB → RGBA): 0.15; more accurate alpha and despill edges.
- Clean-up: 0.05.
- Defocus recovery: 0.10 (together with Charbonnier and highlight damping).
- Degrain and roto: leave at 0.

## Recommended values

Default when the composite loss is switched on by hand: 0.15 for 4-channel output, otherwise 0.05. Input range 0–2.

adv_loss_hdr.title: Highlight damping
adv_loss_hdr.summary: Lowers the error weight by the target's luminance so that large values in highlights do not dominate training. 0 = no damping; RGB only.
adv_loss_hdr.body:
## What it does

Each residual is divided by (1 + luminance)^α, with luminance = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B of the target, so the squared error is weighted by (1 + luminance)^(−2α). A larger α gives highlights less weight; the read-out below the fields lists the weight in shadows, at mid white and in highlights. The alpha channel of a 4-channel output keeps its full weight; for a 1-channel matte α is fixed at 0.

## When to use

The Defocus preset uses 0.5 (together with Charbonnier and the gradient term). Leave it at 0 for other tasks.

## Recommended values

0 (the default when the composite loss is switched on by hand). Input range 0–1.2.

## Limitations

On its own it has no clear effect on accuracy.

adv_loss_eps.title: Smoothing constant
adv_loss_eps.summary: The ε in the Charbonnier term √(residual² + ε²); sets where it changes from squared to absolute error. Only used when the Charbonnier ratio is above 0.
adv_loss_eps.body:
## What it does

For residuals much smaller than ε, Charbonnier behaves like the squared error; for much larger ones like the absolute error.

## Recommended values

1e-3 (default). Linear ACEScg material rarely needs another value.

adv_stages.title: Stage ratios and transition warm-up
adv_stages.summary: Redistributes the steps of the three Multi-Resolution stages (1/4, 1/2, 1/1) and adds a learning-rate warm-up at each stage change. Requires Multi-Resolution.
adv_stages.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat

With Multi-Resolution on, CopyCat splits the total steps into equal thirds and trains at 1/4, 1/2 and 1/1 resolution in turn (crops shrink accordingly, for example 64 → 128 → 256 px). The full-resolution stage gets only the last third, and there is no learning-rate warm-up at a stage change.

## What it does

- [[doc:adv_stages_ratio|Stage shares]]: for example 15 / 25 / 60, which leaves more steps for full resolution.
- [[doc:adv_stages_warmup|Transition warm-up]]: after entering the 1/2 and 1/1 stages, the learning rate rises linearly from 10% to its normal value over the set number of steps.

## When to use

Defocus recovery: such shots make almost no progress at the low-resolution stages and improve mainly at full resolution (the Defocus preset uses 15 / 25 / 60 with a 200-step warm-up). Leave it off (equal thirds) for other tasks.

## Limitations

Full-resolution steps are the slowest, so a larger 1/1 share makes training longer. No effect when Multi-Resolution is Off.

adv_stages_ratio.title: Stage shares
adv_stages_ratio.summary: Percentage of the total steps in the 1/4, 1/2 and 1/1 resolution stages; the three add up to 100%.
adv_stages_ratio.body:
## What it does

Changing one value adjusts the other two so that the total stays 100%; the 1/1 stage keeps at least 5%. The bar below shows the steps per stage together with the steps of CopyCat's equal thirds.

## Recommended values

15 / 25 / 60 for defocus recovery. Other tasks: equal thirds (module off).

adv_stages_warmup.title: Transition warm-up
adv_stages_warmup.summary: Number of steps over which the learning rate rises linearly from 10% back to its normal value after entering the 1/2 and 1/1 stages; 0 = no warm-up.
adv_stages_warmup.body:
## What it does

At a stage change both the crop size and the scale of the image content change; the lower learning rate during the warm-up keeps the weights from jumping. The overall decay of the learning rate (the same polynomial decay as in CopyCat) is unchanged.

## Recommended values

200 steps (the setting of the Defocus preset). Input range 0–5000.

adv_ema.title: Averaged weights (EMA)
adv_ema.summary: Keeps a running average of the weights next to the trained weights; previews, checkpoints and exports use the average. Training itself is unchanged; results are steadier when stopping early or using a mid-run checkpoint.
adv_ema.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat

CopyCat previews, saves and exports the weights of the current step. While the learning rate is still high, the weights move a little from step to step, so stopping early or picking a checkpoint from the middle of the run can catch them at an off moment.

## What it does

The optimiser never reads the average, so the trained weights are exactly the same as without it. Validation, previews, checkpoints, the [[doc:monitor_rec|checkpoint recommendation]] and exported models use the averaged weights. The average restarts at every new resolution stage.

## When to use

When training may be stopped early based on the preview, or a checkpoint from the middle of the run will be used. The difference is largest on keying, clean-up and face-edit shots, whose presets switch it on; on defocus and degrain shots it makes little difference.

## Recommended values

[[doc:adv_ema_decay|Decay β]] 0.9995 (about the average of the last 2000 steps).

## Limitations

For a run trained to the end, averaged and current weights give the same result (the learning rate is then close to 0). In the first, low-resolution stage the average can lag slightly behind. The extra cost per step is small.

adv_ema_decay.title: Decay β
adv_ema_decay.summary: Share of the old average kept at every step: a larger β averages over more steps and is smoother, but follows training more slowly. It is about the average of the last 1 ÷ (1 − β) steps.
adv_ema_decay.body:
## What it does

At every step: average = β × average + (1 − β) × current weights. At the start of each resolution stage β rises from a small value to the set value, so the average catches up with the new stage quickly. The read-out below the field shows the matching number of steps and the half-life.

## Recommended values

0.9995 (default, about 2000 steps). Range 0.9–0.99999.

adv_augment.title: Augmentation (horizontal flip / exposure jitter)
adv_augment.summary: Randomly flips training pairs horizontally and changes their linear exposure, input and target together, to vary the training crops. Off by default and not used by any scene preset.
adv_augment.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat

CopyCat applies no flips or exposure changes.

## What it does

- [[doc:adv_augment_flip|Horizontal flip]]: mirrors an input / target pair left to right with the set probability.
- [[doc:adv_augment_exposure|Exposure jitter]]: multiplies the RGB of input and target by the same 2^EV gain within the set range (alpha unchanged).

Both are applied to the training crops on the GPU; the dataset files are not changed.

## When to use

Only for content without a direction: no text, logos, one-sided lighting or one-way motion.

## Limitations

The effect varies from shot to shot; no scene preset uses this module.

adv_augment_flip.title: Horizontal flip probability
adv_augment_flip.summary: Probability that a training crop is mirrored left to right: 0% (no flip) or 50%. Input and target are always flipped together.
adv_augment_flip.body:
## When to use

Choose 0% when the frame contains text, logos or asymmetric design, or when lighting or motion has a clear direction: mirrored samples never occur in the shot, but the model learns them anyway.

## Recommended values

50% when the module is switched on.

adv_augment_exposure.title: Exposure jitter range
adv_augment_exposure.summary: Range (±EV) of random exposure changes of the training crops: the RGB of input and target is multiplied by the same 2^EV gain. 0 = no change; fixed at 0 when both input and output have fewer than 3 channels.
adv_augment_exposure.body:
## What it does

For every crop a value between −EV and +EV is drawn and the RGB of input and target is multiplied by 2^EV; alpha and 1-channel mattes are unchanged. The gain range is shown next to the field.

## Recommended values

0 EV (default). Input range 0–1.5 EV.

adv_kf_common.title: Keyframe commonality
adv_kf_common.summary: Compares the keyframes before training: only where the other keyframes agree with each other and one keyframe differs, that region of the one keyframe is changed to match. Keyframes that already agree stay as painted.
adv_kf_common.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat

CopyCat treats every keyframe as ground truth. Hand-painted keyframes rarely agree completely: on one of them a region may be painted weaker or stronger, sit a few pixels off, or have its texture redrawn. These differences are learned too, and on the in-between frames the result swims between versions.

## What it does

Before training, the edits of neighbouring keyframes are carried onto each keyframe along the motion of the validation sequence and compared:

- Where the other keyframes agree with each other and only this one differs, this keyframe is changed to match before it is used for training.
- Keyframes that already agree stay as painted.
- Where the keyframes have nothing in common, nothing is changed.

It does not average (averaging would blur detail), does not take one keyframe as the reference and does not create training data on frames without a keyframe; training still uses only the keyframes. The optional [[doc:adv_kf_common_overall|overall look]] setting also pulls the overall brightness and colour of each keyframe towards the consensus of its neighbours.

## When to use

Shots where only a few frames were painted by hand and those keyframes do not fully agree: wounds, blemish clean-up, beauty work, ageing / de-ageing, face-swap touch-up and similar clean-up work. The Face edit preset switches it on.

## Requirements

- An RGB → RGB model (3 → 3).
- A dataset with a [[doc:dataset_validation_sequence|validation sequence]] (the complete plate of the shot) whose frames are the inputs of the keyframes.
- At least 3 keyframes.

If a requirement is not met, the task can still be submitted; training uses the keyframes as painted and the task page states the reason.

## Limitations

Detail that was repainted differently on every keyframe (no version shared by a majority) cannot be corrected. Regions that move too fast to be aligned stay as painted; with very fast motion, alignment errors can slightly change keyframes that already agreed. Training gets one preparation pass before it starts (seconds to a few minutes, depending on the frame size and the length of the validation sequence); the speed of each step is unchanged.

## How to read it

The task page shows a "Keyframe commonality" block: whether it was applied, how many keyframes were compared, how much was rewritten, and a comparison picture (painted keyframe | keyframe used for training | amount of change). Loss and keyframe MSE on the task page are computed against the rewritten keyframes and cannot be compared directly with tasks that do not use this module; the keyframe scores on the Experiments page use the painted keyframes, so rewritten regions count as error there. Judge the effect on the in-between frames: whether the result still swims during playback.

adv_kf_common_threshold.title: Outlier threshold
adv_kf_common_threshold.summary: How far a keyframe must be from the consensus of the other keyframes before it counts as inconsistent and is rewritten. Smaller values rewrite more.
adv_kf_common_threshold.body:
## What it does

The distance is measured in units of how much the other keyframes differ among themselves (a squared distance): at the threshold a region is rewritten halfway, far above it almost completely, far below it hardly at all. How much is rewritten also depends on how well the other keyframes agree with each other.

## Recommended values

2 (default). Range 0.5–16. Raise it when normal differences between keyframes get rewritten; lower it when clearly inconsistent regions are left as they are.

adv_kf_common_span.title: Keyframes compared on each side
adv_kf_common_span.summary: Number of keyframes before and after each keyframe that it is compared with. More keyframes give a broader majority, but distant keyframes with large motion are harder to align.
adv_kf_common_span.body:
## Recommended values

2 (default): each keyframe is compared with up to 2 keyframes on each side, at most 4 in total. Range 1–4. Use more for dense keyframes and little motion, fewer for large motion.

adv_kf_common_overall.title: Overall look to consensus
adv_kf_common_overall.summary: Where the keyframes differ in overall brightness or colour, pulls each one towards the consensus of its neighbours. Acts only on the broad layer without detail, so nothing blurs. Switch it off when the effect is meant to change over the shot (for example a wound that darkens).
adv_kf_common_overall.body:
## What it does

Besides local outliers, keyframes can each differ slightly overall (brightness, colour). Then no majority shares one version, the local rule changes nothing, and the trained result drifts slowly from one keyframe's look to the next. With this setting on, only the broad layer (overall brightness and colour, structures above about 10 px) is pulled towards the consensus of the neighbouring keyframes; a single keyframe whose whole look is off is handled by the local rule and is not averaged into its neighbours. Where the keyframes already agree, nothing changes.

## When to use

On by default. Switch it off when the effect is meant to change over time, for example a wound that darkens or make-up that fades in.

presets_overview.title: Scene presets
presets_overview.summary: Sets the recommended combination for a type of shot in one click: Model Size, channels, Crop Size and the advanced settings. Presets never change Epochs; every value can still be edited after loading.
presets_overview.body:
## What it does

A preset first resets the advanced settings to the Nuke defaults, then sets Model Size, input / output channels, Crop Size (reduced automatically for small frames) and the matching advanced settings, and switches Multi-Resolution on. Epochs, Batch Size and the other basic settings stay as they are. Every value can be changed after loading.

## When to use

Use the preset that matches the type of shot as a starting point. When unsure, use "Nuke defaults (all off)": training is then identical to Nuke CopyCat.

## Limitations

When training continues from an existing checkpoint, Model Size and channels come from the checkpoint and the preset does not change them. The values of each preset are listed on the Scene presets page of the help center.

preset_nuke.title: Nuke defaults (all off)
preset_nuke.summary: Switches every advanced setting off, sets Crop Size to 256 and Multi-Resolution on: training is then identical to the Nuke CopyCat defaults.
preset_nuke.body:
## What it does

Restores CopyCat's way of training: 4 px crop grid from the bottom edge, MSE in linear space, equal resolution stages, no augmentation, no averaged weights and no keyframe commonality. Model Size, channels and Epochs are not changed.

## When to use

To compare directly with a model trained in Nuke, or as the baseline of a comparison.

preset_cleanup_grain.title: Clean-up
preset_cleanup_grain.summary: Local paint-out shots: decals, tracking markers, stains, wires. Uses the 1 px crop grid, the gradient term and averaged weights; Model Size Medium (the Nuke default).
preset_cleanup_grain.body:
## When to use

Removing local elements on a few keyframes: decals, tracking markers, stains, wires, small objects. Most of the frame stays unedited.

## What it does

- [[doc:adv_crop_grid|Crop grid]] 1 px: the effect is largest on this kind of shot and grows with training length.
- [[doc:adv_loss_grad|Gradient term]]: cleaner edges of the repaired region.
- [[doc:adv_ema|Averaged weights]]: steadier results when stopping early or using a mid-run checkpoint.
- Model Size Medium (the Nuke default); Small needs about 2/3 of the training time at lower accuracy.

## Limitations

If the repair is painted differently from keyframe to keyframe, [[doc:adv_kf_common|keyframe commonality]] can be added (requires a validation sequence).

Evidence for the modules: [[ev:adv_crop_grid]] · [[ev:adv_loss_grad]] · [[ev:adv_ema]] · [[ev:model_size]]

preset_keying_despill.title: Keying
preset_keying_despill.summary: Green / blue screen keying with despilled RGB and alpha as output (RGB → RGBA). Uses the 1 px crop grid, the gradient term and averaged weights; Model Size Small.
preset_keying_despill.body:
## When to use

Shots where despilled, premultiplied RGB and an alpha are needed from the RGB plate.

## What it does

- Channels set to RGB → RGBA (3 → 4).
- [[doc:adv_loss_grad|Gradient term]]: more accurate alpha and despill edges.
- [[doc:adv_crop_grid|Crop grid]] 1 px.
- [[doc:adv_ema|Averaged weights]]: steadier results when stopping early or using a mid-run checkpoint.
- Model Size Small.

## Limitations

Keying quality depends on the number of keyframes: the more keyframes cover the motion and the hair, the more accurate the alpha on the in-between frames.

Evidence for the modules: [[ev:adv_loss_grad]] · [[ev:adv_crop_grid]] · [[ev:adv_ema]] · [[ev:dataset_keyframes]]

preset_bokeh_focus.title: Defocus
preset_bokeh_focus.summary: Restores sharpness to out-of-focus shots. Uses a Large model, the 1 px crop grid, the composite loss and stage ratios weighted towards full resolution.
preset_bokeh_focus.body:
## When to use

Shots with missed focus or defocus blur that must be made sharp again, including linear HDR material with strong highlights.

## What it does

- Model Size Large: for this task, larger models do better.
- [[doc:adv_stages|Stage ratios]]: most steps go to the full-resolution stage, where defocus recovery is mainly learned.
- [[doc:adv_loss|Composite loss]]: Charbonnier, gradient term and highlight damping together improve accuracy in display space (sRGB).
- [[doc:adv_crop_grid|Crop grid]] 1 px.

## Limitations

A Large model takes much longer per step than Small, and the stage ratios lengthen the slowest, full-resolution stage, so training takes longer overall.

Evidence for the modules: [[ev:model_size]] · [[ev:adv_stages]] · [[ev:adv_loss_charbonnier]] · [[ev:adv_loss_hdr]] · [[ev:adv_crop_grid]]

preset_degrain_clean.title: Degrain
preset_degrain_clean.summary: Removes film grain and sensor noise. Switches on the 1 px crop grid only; Model Size Small.
preset_degrain_clean.body:
## When to use

Shots where film grain or noise in the shadows must be removed while the original detail is kept.

## What it does

- [[doc:adv_crop_grid|Crop grid]] 1 px.
- Model Size Small: for this task, larger models bring no advantage.
- All other advanced settings stay off: the loss terms make no clear difference here.

## Limitations

Training beyond about 100k Epochs does not improve the result.

Evidence for the modules: [[ev:adv_crop_grid]] · [[ev:model_size]] · [[ev:epochs]]

preset_roto_matte.title: Roto
preset_roto_matte.summary: Single-channel alpha mattes from RGB plates (RGB → Alpha). Sets the channels and the 1 px crop grid; the result depends mostly on the number and spacing of keyframes.
preset_roto_matte.body:
## When to use

Shots that need a matte for a person or an object on every frame.

## What it does

- Channels set to RGB → Alpha (3 → 1).
- [[doc:adv_crop_grid|Crop grid]] 1 px (little effect on this kind of shot).
- Model Size Small: for this task, larger models do worse.
- All other advanced settings stay off.

## Requirements

The farther a frame is from the nearest keyframe, the less accurate the matte; the faster the motion, the denser the keyframes must be, and fast limb motion needs a keyframe every few frames. Adding keyframes helps more than changing any setting.

Evidence for the modules: [[ev:dataset_keyframes]] · [[ev:model_size]] · [[ev:adv_crop_grid]]

preset_face_edit.title: Face edit
preset_face_edit.summary: Face shots such as wounds, blemish clean-up, beauty work, ageing / de-ageing and face-swap touch-up. Uses the 1 px crop grid, Charbonnier 0.25, keyframe commonality and averaged weights; RGB → RGB model, Model Size Medium (the Nuke default).
preset_face_edit.body:
## When to use

Face shots where only a few frames were painted by hand and the painted keyframes do not fully agree: a region painted weaker or stronger, a few pixels off, or with its texture redrawn.

## What it does

- [[doc:adv_kf_common|Keyframe commonality]]: before training, regions of single keyframes that disagree with the other keyframes are changed to match, so the in-between frames no longer swim between versions.
- [[doc:adv_crop_grid|Crop grid]] 1 px.
- [[doc:adv_loss_charbonnier|Charbonnier]] 0.25 (no gradient term, no highlight damping): more accurate unseen frames and edited areas, and clearly fewer changes to the unedited area.
- [[doc:adv_ema|Averaged weights]]: steadier results when stopping early or using a mid-run checkpoint.
- Channels RGB → RGB, Model Size Medium (the Nuke default); Small needs about 2/3 of the training time at lower accuracy.

## Requirements

The dataset needs a [[doc:dataset_validation_sequence|validation sequence]] and at least 3 keyframes. If a requirement is not met, the task can still be submitted; keyframe commonality then has no effect and the task page states the reason.

## Limitations

Detail repainted differently on every keyframe cannot be corrected. When the effect is meant to change over the shot (for example a wound that darkens), switch off [[doc:adv_kf_common_overall|overall look to consensus]] in keyframe commonality.

Evidence: [[ev:preset_face_edit]] · [[ev:adv_kf_common]] · [[ev:adv_crop_grid]] · [[ev:adv_ema]]

lab_overview.title: Experiments
lab_overview.summary: Train several settings on the same dataset in one batch and compare their curves, evaluation metrics and images.
lab_overview.body:
## What it does
**① Plan & Submit**: generate a set of settings with a comparison set, or configure tasks by hand in the training form and add them to an experiment group, then submit the whole group to the training queue.
**② Compare & Analyze**: select existing training tasks to overlay their Loss and Val MSE curves, measure evaluation metrics on the keyframes and the validation sequence, and play their results back in sync.

## When to use
To settle the settings for a shot, for example to compare a scene preset with the Nuke CopyCat defaults, to compare two Model Sizes, or to see what an advanced setting does on this shot.

## Limitations
Tasks compared with each other should use the same dataset and the same Epochs; otherwise the differences do not come only from the setting being compared. Temporary users cannot use the Experiments page.

lab_combo.title: Comparison set
lab_combo.summary: Generates a set of comparison tasks for the selected task type: the recommended configuration (same as the scene preset), variants of it, and a control with the Nuke CopyCat defaults.
lab_combo.body:
## What it does
Builds a set of training settings for the selected task type and adds it to a new experiment group:

- **Recommended**: identical to the matching scene preset; always first.
- **Variants**: most of them change one setting of the recommended configuration (Model Size, gradient term, stage ratios, Crop Size or one advanced setting); each one is described in the list.
- **Control**: the Nuke CopyCat defaults (4 px crop grid, plain MSE, no advanced settings, no early stop) with the same Model Size as the recommended configuration.

Every task uses the Epochs, Batch Size, Mixed Precision, Learning Rate, Seed and Initial Weights currently set in the training form (the control loads no initial weights); Multi-Resolution is always on, and Crop Size and channels are set by the comparison set. If the dataset does not meet the requirements of keyframe commonality, the set does not include it and the panel states why.

## When to use
To find out whether a scene preset works better than the Nuke CopyCat defaults on the current shot, or to choose between a few similar settings. The set can be added to the pending list for review first, or submitted directly.

## How to read it
The estimated time assumes the tasks run in parallel on the available GPUs; with Stop after best score on, an estimate with early stopping is shown next to the time for training every task to its full Epochs.
When the tasks have finished, select the group under **Compare & Analyze**, use the control as the comparison reference and compare the keyframe metrics, the validation-sequence metrics and the in-between frames. Tasks with keyframe commonality rewrite parts of individual keyframes before training; the keyframe metrics count those parts as error, so judge those tasks on the in-between frames.

lab_combo_dataset.title: Test dataset
lab_combo_dataset.summary: The dataset the comparison set trains on: the dataset currently selected in the training form.
lab_combo_dataset.body: Every task of the set trains on this dataset. With a validation sequence, the validation-sequence metrics can be measured when comparing results, and [[doc:auto_extend]] becomes available; without one, only keyframe metrics can be compared. A validation sequence can be attached or replaced here.

lab_combo_task_type.title: Task type
lab_combo_task_type.summary: Decides which scene preset the comparison set uses as its recommended configuration and which variants it generates.
lab_combo_task_type.body:
## What it does
With **Detect from dataset**, the task type set on the dataset is used; if none is set, it is inferred from the channels, the dataset name and the difference between input and Ground Truth. A single-channel output, for example, is treated as Roto. A task type can also be chosen directly.

## Recommended values
Keep **Detect from dataset** when the dataset's task type is correct. If the result does not match the shot, choose the type here, or set the dataset's task type on the Datasets page or in the training form.

lab_combo_scope.title: Set size
lab_combo_scope.summary: Number of tasks in the comparison set: Compact 4, Standard up to 6, All up to 8. The Nuke CopyCat defaults control is always included.
lab_combo_scope.body:
## What it does
Tasks are taken in list order: the recommended configuration first, the control always last, and the variants in between. Some task types have fewer variants, so **All** may give fewer than 8 tasks.

## Recommended values
**Standard**. With little GPU time, **Compact** trains the recommended configuration, the first two variants and the control.

lab_stop_after_best.title: Stop after best score
lab_stop_after_best.summary: Once training reaches the full-resolution stage, stops it when the score has not improved for the set number of Epochs and saves the current checkpoint, which saves GPU time in batch experiments.
lab_stop_after_best.body:
## What it does
In the 1/1 full-resolution stage the model is scored at regular intervals (at least once per Checkpoint Interval). When the score has not exceeded its previous best for the set number of Epochs (a new best has to be at least 0.015 dB higher), the checkpoint is saved, training stops and the GPU is released.

## Score
The score has two parts: how closely the keyframes are reproduced (PSNR of the edited region and of the whole frame, edge error), and how stable the parts that should not change stay (the unedited area of the keyframes; if there is none, the static areas of the validation sequence). For mattes, checkpoints whose foreground clearly disappears are penalised. The score does not measure how the edit carries over to the in-between frames.

## Recommended values
The default depends on the task type: Clean-up 60000, Degrain 80000, all other types 100000 Epochs. When off, every task trains to its full Epochs. The Nuke CopyCat defaults control never stops early.

## Limitations
In-between frames can still improve after the fit to the keyframes has levelled off, so a task that stopped early may end before its best point. Train to the full Epochs for final deliverables.

lab_group_name.title: Experiment group name
lab_group_name.summary: Name of the experiment group the comparison set is added to; if empty, a name is generated from the task type and the number of tasks.
lab_group_name.body: After submission the tasks appear under this group name in **Compare & Analyze**, where the whole group can be selected at once. The name can be edited in the pending list before submission and renamed afterwards.

lab_native_baseline.title: Nuke defaults control
lab_native_baseline.summary: Adds a training task with exactly the Nuke CopyCat defaults to the current experiment group, as the reference for comparison.
lab_native_baseline.body:
The task uses the current dataset with Model Size Medium, Multi-Resolution on, Batch Size Auto, Crop Size 256, Mixed Precision Adaptive, no initial weights, no advanced settings and no early stop; Epochs, channels, Learning Rate and Seed are taken from the form.
The control of a comparison set differs from it: there, the Model Size is the same as in the recommended configuration.

lab_note.title: Note
lab_note.summary: A short description attached to a task when it is added to an experiment group; shown in the pending list and in the task list of Compare & Analyze.
lab_note.body: Use it to record how this task differs from the others, for example "control" or "1 px crop grid + gradient 0.05". Tasks generated by a comparison set get their description automatically.

lab_staged_groups.title: Pending experiment groups
lab_staged_groups.summary: Training tasks that have not been submitted yet, arranged in experiment groups; each group can be submitted on its own, or all groups at once.
lab_staged_groups.body:
## What it does
- **Add current settings to list** adds the current settings of the training form to the current group; **Add Nuke defaults control** adds a task with the Nuke CopyCat defaults.
- Each task can be renamed, reordered, moved to another group, or loaded back into the form with **Load into form** for changes.
- **Submit to** decides whether the submitted tasks form a new experiment group or are appended to an existing one.
- Submitted tasks enter the training queue and start as GPUs become free; their progress is shown below the list.

## Limitations
The pending list is stored in this browser only; it is not available in another browser or after the browser data is cleared.

lab_compare_tasks.title: Tasks to compare
lab_compare_tasks.summary: Select the training tasks to compare; tasks are listed by experiment group and can be selected across groups or a whole group at once.
lab_compare_tasks.body:
## What it does
- Selected tasks appear in the curves, the metrics table and the sequence viewer on the right, each in its own colour.
- **This group only** selects just this group and uses its task with the Nuke CopyCat defaults as the comparison reference (or the first task if there is none).
- Tasks submitted from the Experiments page are listed by experiment group; individually created training tasks are listed under **Ungrouped** and can be selected as well.
- Tasks can be moved to another group or reordered within it; groups can be created, renamed, reordered or dissolved (their tasks become ungrouped).
- The list can be sorted manually or by keyframe PSNR, HFI or Val MSE.

lab_compare_baseline.title: Comparison reference (Δ)
lab_compare_baseline.summary: The task the others are compared with in the metrics table; the small figure under each value is the difference from the reference, green when better and red when worse.
lab_compare_baseline.body: If none is set, the first selected task is the reference; usually the task with the Nuke CopyCat defaults is used. The high-frequency change index (HFI) has no better or worse direction, so its differences are not coloured. The best value of each column is shown in bold green (except HFI).

lab_param_tags.title: Parameter tags
lab_param_tags.summary: Short tags under a task's name that list the parameters in which the task differs from the Nuke CopyCat defaults.
lab_param_tags.body:
Tasks marked **Nuke CopyCat defaults** use the CopyCat defaults. Tags:

- `Small` / `Large`: Model Size (the default Medium is not shown).
- `Crop=384`, `Batch=4`, `MultiRes=Off`, `FP16` / `FP32`: the corresponding basic parameters.
- `20000ep`: Epochs (not shown for 10000); `…st`: total steps (tasks that recorded steps only).
- `Init=…`: Initial Weights.
- `Grid=1px`, `Grid=4px·Top`: step and anchor of the crop grid.
- `Charb(0.25)`, `0.05∇`, `HDR(0.5)`: Charbonnier, gradient term and highlight damping of the composite loss.
- `Stage(15/25/60)`: stage ratios.
- `EMA(0.9995)`: averaged weights and their decay.
- `Aug(Flip(0.5)/EV±0.25)`: augmentation.
- `KfCommon(thr=2,span=2)`: keyframe commonality; `raft` = RAFT optical flow, `no-overall` = the overall-look option is off.
- `OptStop(+60000ep)`: Stop after best score.

lab_eval.title: Keyframe and validation-sequence evaluation
lab_eval.summary: Runs each selected task's checkpoint on the keyframes and the validation sequence, measures the values of the metrics table and renders the frames of the sequence viewer.
lab_eval.body:
## What it does
- **Keyframe metrics**: each task's training keyframes are inferred and compared with their Ground Truth: keyframe PSNR, edge gradient error, unedited-area drift and P99 error.
- **Validation-sequence metrics**: when there is a validation sequence, every frame of it is inferred: edit-layer frame-to-frame change, HFI and static-area boiling; the result and a heat map of every frame are saved. The validation sequence has no ground truth, so these metrics describe temporal stability, not accuracy.

Tasks that were measured before show their stored results; **Re-measure** measures them again.

## Requirements
Each task needs at least one saved checkpoint. Without a validation sequence only the keyframe metrics are measured, and the per-frame curves, validation-sequence metrics and viewer are unavailable; attach a validation sequence to the dataset, or choose another dataset with one under **Evaluation dataset and sequence**.

## Limitations
The keyframes are the frames the model was trained on, so keyframe metrics describe the fit, not the result on in-between frames. Tasks trained with keyframe commonality are measured against the original keyframes, so the parts rewritten before training count as error.

lab_eval_dataset.title: Evaluation dataset and sequence
lab_eval_dataset.summary: Chooses the validation sequence the selected tasks are evaluated on; by default it follows the selected tasks' training dataset. Keyframe metrics are always measured on each task's own keyframes.
lab_eval_dataset.body:
- **Follow the selected tasks' dataset** (recommended): uses the validation sequence of the dataset the selected tasks were trained on; if they come from different datasets, the first one that can be identified is used.
- **A specific dataset**: every selected task is run on this dataset's validation sequence. Datasets with a validation sequence and separately uploaded evaluation sequences (plate frames only, no keyframes) can be chosen.

The choice does not affect the keyframe metrics.

lab_eval_weights.title: Evaluated checkpoint
lab_eval_weights.summary: Which checkpoint of each task is evaluated: the one with the lowest Val MSE, or the latest saved one.
lab_eval_weights.body:
- **Lowest Val MSE**: the step with the lowest [[doc:metric_val_mse]] during training (default).
- **Latest**: the last saved checkpoint; for a task that trained to the end, the final step.

For a task that trained to the end, the final step is usually the best checkpoint; choose **Latest** to compare the models that will be delivered. The **Checkpoint step** column of the metrics table shows the step that was used.

lab_chart.title: Curve overlay
lab_chart.summary: Overlays the training curves or per-frame curves of the selected tasks in one graph, in the same colours as the task list.
lab_chart.body:
- **Loss** and **Val MSE**: plotted over training steps; see [[doc:metric_loss]] and [[doc:metric_val_mse]]. A logarithmic scale can be switched on, and the Loss curve can be smoothed.
- **Per-frame HFI**, **per-frame edit change (ΔR)** and **per-frame PSNR**: plotted over the frames of the validation sequence; available after an evaluation. Clicking a frame on the curve shows it in the sequence viewer.

Hovering shows each task's value at that position.

lab_viewer.title: Synchronized sequence viewer
lab_viewer.summary: Plays the selected tasks' results on the validation sequence side by side, with zoom, pan and frame number kept in sync.
lab_viewer.body:
- **Result**: the model output in sRGB (OCIO); outputs with alpha are shown over a checkerboard.
- **Frame-change heat map (×12)**: the change of the edit layer from the previous frame, amplified 12 times and laid over the darkened plate; brighter means more change between frames at that point.
- **Ground-truth error heat map (×10)**: available when the sequence has per-frame ground truth; shows the difference from it, amplified 10 times.

**Show plate** adds the validation sequence itself as the first column; **Jump to largest change** moves to the frame with the largest edit-layer change. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan; FPS sets the playback speed.

lab_db.title: Results database
lab_db.summary: Parameters, training curves and evaluation results of every training task are kept in a local results database and can be exported as CSV.
lab_db.body: The summary bar shows the number of tasks, evaluations and curve points in the database. **Export database CSV** exports the parameters, best Val MSE, keyframe PSNR and validation-sequence metrics of all tasks; **Export CSV** above the metrics table exports only the selected tasks and their comparison values. Archiving a task keeps its curves and evaluation values in the database.

lab_archive.title: Archive
lab_archive.summary: Frees the disk space of the selected tasks: curves and evaluation values are written to the results database first, then preview images, evaluation frames and the checkpoints used to resume training are deleted. Exported model files are kept.
lab_archive.body:
## What it does
Deleted: full-frame previews, contact sheets, the sequence frames and heat maps of evaluations, and the intermediate checkpoints used to resume training. Kept: the exported model files and all parameters, curves and evaluation values. Tasks that are training or queued are not archived.

## Limitations
An archived task cannot be extended any more. To view its sequence frames again, use **Re-measure** in Compare & Analyze to render them anew.

metric_val_mse.title: Keyframe MSE (Val MSE)
metric_val_mse.summary: Mean squared error over the whole frame of every keyframe, computed at every checkpoint. Lower means the keyframes are reproduced more accurately.
metric_val_mse.body:
## What it does
At every [[doc:checkpoint_interval]], each keyframe is inferred over the whole frame with the current weights and compared with its Ground Truth; the mean squared error of the linear ACEScg values is averaged over all keyframes. With [[doc:adv_ema]] on, the averaged weights are used.

## How to read it
- Shown in the progress row, on the loss curve (green dots) and in the model version list; the "Lowest keyframe MSE" tag marks the version with the lowest value.
- Unlike the Loss, it is computed on whole frames at full resolution and does not depend on the resolution stage.
- "Best Val MSE" on the Experiments page is the lowest value during the task's training.

## Limitations
It measures the training keyframes only, not the in-between frames. Check those on the validation sequence or in Nuke. With [[doc:adv_kf_common]] on, the targets are the keyframes as rewritten before training.

metric_psnr_srgb.title: Keyframe PSNR (sRGB)
metric_psnr_srgb.summary: Peak signal-to-noise ratio between the model output and the keyframe Ground Truth in sRGB display space, in dB, averaged over all keyframes; higher means closer.
metric_psnr_srgb.body:
## How to read it
Output and Ground Truth are converted to sRGB display values (0–1) with OCIO, then PSNR = 10·log₁₀(1 ÷ MSE). PSNR in display space is closer to how errors in shadows and mid-tones are perceived. +3 dB roughly halves the mean squared error; +10 dB reduces it to one tenth.

## Limitations
Measured on the training keyframes only, so it describes the fit. When the edited region is small, the whole-frame PSNR is dominated by the unedited area; read it together with the unedited-area drift and the images.

metric_edge.title: Edge gradient error
metric_edge.summary: Mean absolute difference between the spatial gradients (neighbouring-pixel differences) of the output and the keyframe Ground Truth, in ‰ (linear value 1.0 = 1000 ‰); lower means edges and detail are closer to the target.
metric_edge.body:
## How to read it
The horizontal and vertical neighbouring-pixel differences of output and Ground Truth are compared and the absolute difference is averaged (linear ACEScg, all channels). It responds to the sharpness of hair, edges and texture: blurring or ringing raises it.

## Limitations
Measured on the training keyframes only.

metric_bg_drift.title: Unedited-area drift
metric_bg_drift.summary: How much the output changes the parts of the keyframes where Ground Truth equals the input (the unedited area), in ‰ (linear value 1.0 = 1000 ‰); should stay close to 0.
metric_bg_drift.body:
## How to read it
The unedited area is every pixel where Ground Truth and input differ by less than 0.0001 in all channels. A rising value means the model alters picture that should stay untouched, for example a colour cast or a grey veil over black areas.

## Requirements
Computed only when the unedited area covers at least 5 % of the frame and input and Ground Truth have the same channels (not for RGB → Alpha, for example).

metric_p99.title: P99 error
metric_p99.summary: 99th percentile of the per-pixel absolute error on the keyframes, in ‰ (linear value 1.0 = 1000 ‰); describes the worst 1 % of pixels, lower is better.
metric_p99.body:
## How to read it
The mean absolute error of each pixel (linear ACEScg, all channels) is computed, its 99th percentile is taken and the result is averaged over all keyframes. When average errors are similar, P99 reveals local artefacts, ringing or missed spots.

## Limitations
Measured on the training keyframes only.

metric_seq_delta.title: Edit-layer frame-to-frame change (ΔR)
metric_seq_delta.summary: On the validation sequence, the average change of the model's edit layer (output − input) between neighbouring frames, in ‰ (sRGB display value 1.0 = 1000 ‰); lower means a temporally steadier edit.
metric_seq_delta.body:
## How to read it
Edit layer δ = output − input (sRGB display values; for mattes the output alpha itself). ΔR = mean|δₜ − δₜ₋₁|, averaged over the whole validation sequence. Subtracting the input removes most of the plate's own change, so what remains is mainly the frame-to-frame jumping of the edit; an edit that legitimately moves with the subject also raises the value, so check the frame-change heat map in the viewer.
The **Largest change** column gives the frame with the highest ΔR; click it to jump there.

## Limitations
The validation sequence has no ground truth: ΔR describes stability, not correctness. A model that changes nothing also has a low ΔR.

metric_hfi.title: High-frequency change index (HFI)
metric_hfi.summary: Mean second-order temporal difference of the edit layer on the validation sequence, in ‰ (sRGB display value 1.0 = 1000 ‰); it follows how much grain the model alters and how much the picture moves. It is not a flicker measure, has no better or worse direction and takes no part in any automatic decision.
metric_hfi.body:
## How to read it
HFI = mean|δₜ − 2δₜ₋₁ + δₜ₋₂|, δ = output − input. Tasks that alter the original grain, such as degrain or denoise, naturally raise it; so does strong subject motion.

## Limitations
Use it only as a reference between tasks of the same shot and task type, not to decide which result is better. Checkpoint recommendation, early stopping and auto-extend do not use it.

metric_static_boil.title: Static-area boiling
metric_static_boil.summary: Average change of the output between neighbouring frames in the parts of the validation sequence where the plate hardly moves, in ‰ (sRGB display value 1.0 = 1000 ‰); ideally close to 0.
metric_static_boil.body:
## How to read it
Static areas are the pixels whose plate value changes by less than 0.005 (sRGB display value) from the previous frame. The output should not change there; a rising value means the result flickers or boils on a static background.

## Requirements
Computed only when static areas cover at least 2 % of the frame.

metric_seq_psnr.title: Per-frame PSNR (validation sequence)
