metric_seq_psnr.summary: PSNR (sRGB, dB) between the output and the ground truth of each frame of the validation sequence; available only when the sequence has per-frame ground truth.
metric_seq_psnr.body: A validation sequence usually holds plate frames only, without per-frame ground truth; this view is then not offered, and the edit-layer change, static-area boiling and the sequence viewer are used instead.

dataset_overview.title: Dataset
dataset_overview.summary: The set of keyframes a model is trained on. Each keyframe is an Input image and the artist's Ground Truth for it; a validation sequence of the shot can be attached.
dataset_overview.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
The image pairs connected to the **Input** and **Ground Truth** inputs of the CopyCat node.

## What it does
A dataset contains:
- **Keyframe Input**: original frames picked from the shot.
- **Keyframe Ground Truth**: the finished version of the same frames, one per Input and at the same resolution. See [[doc:dataset_keyframes]].
- **Validation sequence (optional)**: the complete original plate of the shot; it is not used for training. See [[doc:dataset_validation_sequence]].

All uploaded images are stored as linear ACEScg, 16-bit half-float EXR. The Datasets page lets you scrub through keyframes and the validation sequence and set the task type.

## When to use
Every training task uses one dataset; the same dataset can be used for any number of trainings and experiment comparisons.

dataset_keyframes.title: Keyframes (Input / Ground Truth)
dataset_keyframes.summary: The training image pairs: the Input is an original frame of the shot, the Ground Truth is the finished version of that frame. The model learns the change from Input to Ground Truth.
dataset_keyframes.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
The **Input** / **Ground Truth** image pairs of CopyCat.

## Requirements
- Input and Ground Truth have the same number of images, paired in file-name order; with the material check on, the frame numbers in the file names are compared as well, for example sh010_0101.exr with sh010_0101.exr.
- Both images of a pair have the same resolution, and all keyframes of a dataset have the same resolution.
- Input is RGB or RGBA; Ground Truth is RGB, RGBA or a single-channel alpha. RGBA images whose alpha is 1 everywhere are treated as RGB.
- With the advanced setting Keyframe commonality, every keyframe Input must be a frame of the validation sequence.

## Recommended values
Place keyframes where the shot looks most different: large turns, expression changes, before and after occlusions. Fast and strongly changing shots need more keyframes; roto and keying shots depend most on the number of keyframes.

## Limitations
Differences in how the keyframes were painted are learned as well. The advanced setting Keyframe commonality learns only what the keyframes agree on.

dataset_validation_sequence.title: Validation sequence
dataset_validation_sequence.summary: The complete original plate of the shot, stored with the dataset. It is not used for training; it enables quality monitoring of the in-between frames, checkpoint recommendation, keyframe commonality and sequence evaluation in Experiments.
dataset_validation_sequence.body:
## What it does
A dataset with a validation sequence enables:
- the training quality (in-between frames) card on the task page;
- checkpoint recommendation ([[doc:monitor_rec]]) and auto-extend ([[doc:auto_extend]]);
- the advanced setting Keyframe commonality;
- full-sequence inference and sequence metrics in Experiments.

## Requirements
- Same resolution as the keyframes, at least 2 frames, ordered by file name.
- Keyframe commonality also needs every keyframe Input to be a frame of the validation sequence, and an RGB → RGB model.

## When to use
Upload it whenever the full plate is available. It can be added when the dataset is created, or later on the Datasets page, where it can also be replaced or removed; the keyframes are not affected.

## Limitations
The validation sequence is not used for training and does not change the trained model.

dataset_task_type.title: Task type
dataset_task_type.summary: The compositing task of the dataset: Clean-up, Keying, Defocus, Degrain, Roto or Face edit. Experiments use it to pick the matching scene preset as the starting point of a comparison set.
dataset_task_type.body:
## What it does
- The [[doc:lab_combo|comparison set]] in Experiments starts from the scene preset of this type.
- The dataset picker can filter by task type.
- When a new dataset is set to Roto or Keying, the tolerance switches to Alpha matte (no pixel-difference check).

The task type itself changes no training parameter.

## Recommended values
Choose the type of work done in the shot. If it is left unspecified, Experiments infer it from the channels (RGB → Alpha is treated as Roto, RGB → RGBA as Keying), the dataset name and the mean difference between Input and Ground Truth.

## Limitations
It can be changed on the Datasets page at any time; finished trainings are not affected.

dataset_input_colorspace.title: Input colour space
dataset_input_colorspace.summary: The colour space of the uploaded images. Images are converted to linear ACEScg when they are stored; Auto matches the default behaviour of the Nuke Read node.
dataset_input_colorspace.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
Corresponds to the **colorspace** of the Nuke Read node. Training runs in linear ACEScg.

## What it does
- **Auto (default)**: .exr is taken as linear ACEScg and stored unchanged; .png / .jpg / .tif are taken as sRGB and converted to ACEScg.
- **ACEScg**: every file is taken as linear ACEScg; no conversion.
- **sRGB**: every file is taken as sRGB and converted to ACEScg.
- **Raw**: values are kept as they are; for non-colour data.

Single-channel mattes and alpha channels are always stored as linear values.

## Recommended values
Use Auto. EXR material should be linear ACEScg; convert other gamuts in Nuke first.

dataset_check.title: Material check
dataset_check.summary: Checks, when a dataset is created, that keyframe Inputs and Ground Truths are paired correctly: missing frames, frame numbers, shifted frames, identical files on both sides and excessive pixel differences. On by default.

dataset_tolerance.title: Tolerance
dataset_tolerance.summary: The largest mean pixel difference between Input and Ground Truth that the material check accepts, in percent. If any keyframe pair exceeds it, the dataset is not created.
dataset_tolerance.body:
## What it does
The mean pixel difference is the average absolute difference between Input and Ground Truth, as a percentage of full scale (linear value 1.0), measured on the RGB channels. A very large difference usually means a wrong shot, or an Input and Ground Truth that are not the same frame.

## Recommended values
- **Standard** (35%, default): most clean-up, paint and grading shots.
- **Loose** (50%): shots with very large changes.
- **Strict** (15%): shots with very small changes, such as degrain or small paint-outs.
- **Alpha matte**: for matte targets; no pixel-difference or shifted-frame check. Selected automatically when the task type is Roto or Keying.

The number field accepts any percentage from 5 to 95.

## Requirements
Applies only when the material check is on.

dataset_eval_sequence.title: Evaluation sequence (Input only)
dataset_eval_sequence.summary: A stand-alone sequence of Input frames without keyframes, used in Experiments to run trained models over a whole sequence and measure sequence metrics. It cannot be used for training.
dataset_eval_sequence.body:
## What it does
When it is chosen as the evaluation dataset in the Experiments analysis, the selected models run over the whole sequence and sequence metrics such as frame-to-frame change are measured. There is no Ground Truth, so no keyframe error is computed.

## Requirements
At least 2 frames.

## Limitations
It cannot be used for training. To keep the plate together with a dataset, use its [[doc:dataset_validation_sequence]].

dataset_name.title: Dataset name
dataset_name.summary: The name shown in the dataset list, the training settings and Experiments. Letters, digits, underscores, hyphens and dots can be used.
dataset_name.body:
## What it does
Other characters are replaced by underscores. Names are unique within the workspace: uploading with an existing name replaces that dataset with the new content.

## Recommended values
Use the shot number or name, for example sh010_cleanup.

dataset_files.title: File formats and limits
dataset_files.summary: .exr, .png, .tif / .tiff and .jpg / .jpeg images are supported, or a .zip file containing them. Everything is stored as linear ACEScg, 16-bit half-float EXR.
dataset_files.body:
## Requirements
- At most 300 files each for Input, Ground Truth and the validation sequence; at most 128 MB per file; width and height of an image at most 8192 px.
- At most 512 MB per upload.
- All images of a group have the same resolution.

## Recommended values
Use linear ACEScg EXR, the same data as in Nuke. 8-bit PNG / JPG have limited precision in highlights and shadows.

## Limitations
Data is stored as 16-bit half float; 32-bit float input is reduced to half-float precision.

dataset_demo.title: Demo datasets
dataset_demo.summary: Datasets that ship with the software. They can be used directly for training and experiments, to learn the workflow and to compare settings.
dataset_demo.body:
## What it does
The demo datasets cover common compositing tasks. The description on each card lists the source of the material, the number of keyframes and whether a validation sequence is included.

## When to use
Deleted demo datasets can be added again with Restore Demo Datasets on the Datasets page; this does not affect uploaded datasets.

admin_max_jobs_per_gpu.title: Concurrent tasks per GPU
admin_max_jobs_per_gpu.summary: How many training tasks run on one GPU at the same time, 1–4, default 1. Further tasks wait in the queue.
admin_max_jobs_per_gpu.body:
## What it does
Submitted tasks are assigned to free GPUs in queue order; once a GPU runs this many tasks, the next task waits for another GPU or for a running task to finish.

## Recommended values
Keep 1. Tasks that share a GPU each run slower, the total time rarely gets shorter, and GPU memory can run out.

admin_gpu_pool.title: GPUs and primary / secondary roles
admin_gpu_pool.summary: Selects the GPUs used for training and assigns the primary and secondary GPU: the primary takes training tasks first, the secondary runs full-frame preview and validation first.
admin_gpu_pool.body:
## What it does
- **Enable / disable**: a disabled GPU receives no new tasks and is not used for previews; running tasks finish. If every GPU is disabled, queued tasks wait.
- **Primary**: queued training tasks go to the primary GPU first.
- **Secondary**: takes parallel tasks when the primary is full; while the primary trains, the secondary runs its full-frame preview and validation first, so they take no training time from the primary.
- **Worker**: the other enabled GPUs, which take tasks in turn.

Whether a task sends its preview to the secondary GPU is set by [[doc:preview_gpu]] in the training settings.

## Requirements
A secondary GPU needs at least 2 enabled GPUs; with only one enabled GPU, that GPU is the primary.

## Recommended values
Make the fastest GPU the primary.

admin_temp_restrictions.title: Temporary-user restrictions
admin_temp_restrictions.summary: When on, accounts without granted permissions are temporary users: limited in tasks, Epochs and uploads, and without Experiments or the API. When off, no user is restricted.
admin_temp_restrictions.body:
## What it does
Visitors need no registration: a workspace is created when the page is first opened. With restrictions on, every user except administrators and users holding both the Experiments and the API permission is a temporary user:
- the number of training tasks and the Epochs per task are limited by quotas, see [[doc:admin_default_quotas]];
- the number of uploaded datasets (twice the task quota, at least 4) and their total size (2 GB) are limited;
- Experiments and the API key are unavailable unless granted in the user list.

With restrictions off, every user can use every feature without quotas.

## When to use
Turn it on when the service is open to the public; turn it off for in-house team use.

admin_default_quotas.title: Default quotas for temporary users
admin_default_quotas.summary: The maximum number of training tasks a new temporary user can submit, and the maximum Epochs per task.
admin_default_quotas.body:
## What it does
- **Task limit**: how many training tasks a temporary user can submit in total.
- **Epochs limit**: the largest Epochs value allowed for one task.

Save Defaults applies to temporary users created afterwards; Save and Apply to Existing Temporary Users also updates the existing ones. Quotas of single users can be changed in the user list, see [[doc:admin_user_quota]].

## Requirements
Applies only while temporary-user restrictions are on.

admin_storage_root.title: Data and cache directory
admin_storage_root.summary: Where uploaded datasets, training results, task configurations and the preview cache are stored. It can be an absolute path on a large volume and takes effect immediately.
admin_storage_root.body:
## What it does
The root directory contains:
- `users/`: uploaded datasets;
- `run/`: training results, including checkpoints, exported models, preview and evaluation images;
- `config/`: task configurations;
- `cache/`: thumbnail cache of the web page.

The analytics database stays in the program folder. Leave the path empty to use the default directory.

## When to use
When the disk of the default directory runs out of space, point it to a large volume. With migration checked, existing datasets and training results are moved to the new directory; without it, files in the old directory remain readable.

## Requirements
The directory must be writable and must not lie inside the program or runtime folders. Migration requires that no training or evaluation task is running.

admin_analytics_db.title: Analytics database
admin_analytics_db.summary: The SQLite database holding the parameters, experiment groups, training curves and evaluation metrics of all training tasks; it can be exported as CSV or JSON.
admin_analytics_db.body:
## What it does
The tiles show the number of tasks, experiment groups, curve points, evaluations and per-frame metrics. The export contains the data of all users for analysis in a spreadsheet or a script. Archiving tasks in Experiments deletes cached images; the numbers stay in the database.

admin_users.title: User management
admin_users.summary: Manages workspace accounts: roaming recovery codes, enabling and disabling, quotas and permissions, opening a user's workspace and deleting users.
admin_users.body:
## What it does
- **Create user**: the username can be left empty; one is generated (U-XXXXXX) together with a roaming recovery code. Permissions can be granted in advance.
- **Roaming recovery code**: lets a user restore their workspace on another computer. It can be copied or regenerated; regenerating invalidates the old code immediately.
- **Status**: a disabled user cannot access their workspace.
- **Open workspace**: view the user's tasks and datasets as that user.
- **Delete**: deletes the user with all tasks and datasets; this cannot be undone.

Quotas and permissions: see [[doc:admin_user_quota]] and [[doc:admin_user_permissions]].

admin_user_quota.title: User quota
admin_user_quota.summary: A user's task quota (submitted / limit) and the maximum Epochs per task. Applies to temporary users only.
admin_user_quota.body:
## What it does
- **Task quota**: submitted tasks on the left, the limit on the right; Reset sets the submitted count to 0.
- **Epochs limit**: the largest Epochs value this user may set for a task.

Changes are saved immediately. Administrators have no quota.

## Requirements
Applies only while temporary-user restrictions are on, see [[doc:admin_temp_restrictions]].

admin_user_permissions.title: Permissions
admin_user_permissions.summary: Grants a user the Experiments and API features. Users holding both permissions are not restricted as temporary users.
admin_user_permissions.body:
## What it does
- **Experiments**: use the Experiments page, including comparison sets, batch training and result comparison.
- **API**: use the API key with the /api/v1 interface, see [[doc:api_key]].

While temporary-user restrictions are off, every user can use every feature and the list shows Restrictions off.

api_key.title: API Key
api_key.summary: The key for using the HTTP interface (/api/v1) as the current user: uploading datasets, submitting training and downloading models. Send it in the X-API-Key request header.
api_key.body:
## What it does
The key belongs to the current workspace; whoever holds it can work with all tasks and datasets of that workspace, so keep it private. Regenerating it invalidates the old key immediately. The interface is described in the API documentation (/docs).

## Requirements
Not available to temporary users; an administrator has to grant the API permission, see [[doc:admin_user_permissions]].

monitor_pause_resume.title: Pause and resume
monitor_pause_resume.summary: Pauses a running task and saves its progress so that it can continue from that step later; a queued task can be removed from the queue.
monitor_pause_resume.body:
## What it does
- **Pause Training**: saves a checkpoint at the current step, stops and frees the GPU.
- **Remove from Queue**: takes a queued task out of the queue; nothing is saved.
- **Resume**: puts the task back in the queue and continues from the last saved step up to the total number of steps. The button shows "steps done → total steps".
- **Re-queue**: shown when the task has no usable checkpoint; training starts again from step 0.

## Limitations
A resumed task keeps all of its settings. To train longer, use [[doc:monitor_extend]].

monitor_extend.title: Extend to Epochs
monitor_extend.summary: Sets a higher target Epochs for a started or finished task and continues training from its last saved checkpoint.
monitor_extend.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
Equivalent to raising Epochs in CopyCat and using Resume Training.

## What it does
Enter the new target Epochs (it must be higher than the current value). The total number of steps is recalculated as ⌈Epochs × keyframes ÷ Batch Size⌉ and shown next to the field.
- While training: the current progress is saved and the task re-enters the end of the queue with the new target.
- Paused or finished: the task re-enters the queue with the new target.

## Limitations
- With Multi-Resolution on, the three resolution stages are divided again over the new total number of steps; training continues in the stage the current step falls into, which can be a lower resolution stage.
- Accounts with an Epochs limit cannot go beyond it.

monitor_download.title: Download models
monitor_download.summary: Downloads the model files saved by this task: the latest version, a chosen version or all versions in one ZIP file.
monitor_download.body:
## What it does
- **Download Latest (.pt)**: the last saved version.
- **Download All Models**: every saved version in one ZIP file.
- Each row of the model version list can be downloaded on its own.

File names are the same as in Nuke CopyCat (`Training_YYMMDD_HHMMSS.<step>.pt`); the format is TorchScript.

## Requirements
In Nuke, convert the .pt file to .cat with the **CatFileCreator** node, then use it in the **Inference** node.

monitor_delete.title: Delete task
monitor_delete.summary: Deletes the task and all of its files on the server, including models, previews and the log. This cannot be undone.
monitor_delete.body:
## What it does
A confirmation is required. Download any model you want to keep before deleting.

monitor_progress.title: Training progress (Epoch / Step)
monitor_progress.summary: Epochs and steps completed so far, and their share of the total number of steps.
monitor_progress.body:
## How to read it
`Epoch current / target · Step current / total (percent)`.
- Total steps = ⌈Epochs × keyframes ÷ Batch Size⌉, see [[doc:epochs]].
- The Epoch shown = ⌊current step × Epochs ÷ total steps⌋.

monitor_stage.title: Resolution stage
monitor_stage.summary: The resolution stage the training is in: 1/4, 1/2 or 1/1 (full resolution). Stages exist only with Multi-Resolution on.
monitor_stage.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
The same as CopyCat's Multi-Resolution training: training starts on frames scaled to 1/4, continues at 1/2 and ends at the original resolution (1/1); the crops are 1/4, 1/2 and the full Crop Size. By default the three stages have the same number of steps; the ratio can be changed with the advanced setting [[doc:adv_stages]]. See [[doc:multi_resolution]].

## How to read it
At a stage change the Loss jumps and the speed drops noticeably (each step is slowest at 1/1). Vertical lines on the loss curve mark the changes.

monitor_speed.title: Training speed (steps/s)
monitor_speed.summary: Training steps completed per second, measured between the two most recent log entries.
monitor_speed.body:
## How to read it
The speed depends on the GPU, Model Size, Batch Size and the current resolution stage: the 1/4 stage is fastest, the 1/1 stage slowest. Within a stage it stays steady; previews and checkpoint saves cause short dips.

monitor_eta.title: Time remaining
monitor_eta.summary: Estimated time needed to complete the remaining steps.
monitor_eta.body:
## How to read it
Estimated from the current speed and the speed of this GPU in each resolution stage. Later stages are slower per step; the estimate is corrected automatically as training progresses.

monitor_queue.title: Queue status
monitor_queue.summary: The task's position in the queue, the number of tasks ahead, the estimated wait and the estimated training time.
monitor_queue.body:
## What it does
Each GPU runs one training task at a time; other tasks wait in the order they were submitted and start automatically when a GPU becomes free. The lower part of the panel lists the task running on each GPU and its remaining time.

## How to read it
The estimated wait is based on the remaining time of the tasks ahead; the estimated training time on this task's settings and the speed of the GPU.

metric_loss.title: Loss
metric_loss.summary: Training error: the difference between the model output and the Ground Truth on random crops at the current resolution stage. Lower means closer to the keyframes.
metric_loss.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
The same Loss CopyCat shows during training: the mean squared error (MSE) on linear ACEScg values. With the advanced setting [[doc:adv_loss]] on, the Loss is the weighted sum of its terms.

## How to read it
- Recorded every [[doc:log_interval]]; the progress row and the loss curve show the latest value.
- Each resolution stage uses a different frame and crop size, so the Loss jumps at every stage change and values of different stages cannot be compared directly.
- The Loss describes the fit on random crops only; the error over whole keyframes is [[doc:metric_val_mse]].

monitor_failed.title: Training failure
monitor_failed.summary: When a task fails, shows the error message and the Python traceback; it can be copied, or the settings can be loaded to train again.
monitor_failed.body:
## What it does
- **Copy Error Message**: copies the full error message for troubleshooting.
- **Load Settings and Retry**: loads the task's name, dataset, Initial Weights and training settings into the training form to adjust and submit again.

When the GPU runs out of memory, lower Crop Size or Batch Size and train again.

monitor_kfc.title: Keyframe commonality report
monitor_kfc.summary: Shows what keyframe commonality did to the keyframes before training: whether it was applied, how many keyframes were compared and how much of the edited region was rewritten.
monitor_kfc.body:
## What it does
Tasks with the advanced setting [[doc:adv_kf_common]] on produce this report before training starts:
- **Applied / Not applied**: when not applied, the reason is shown; training uses the keyframes as painted and the result is the same as with the setting off.
- **Comparison**: the number of keyframes compared, the frames of the validation sequence, the optical flow used and the preparation time.
- **Rewritten share** and **keyframe agreement**: see [[doc:metric_kfc_rewritten]] and [[doc:metric_kfc_common]].
- **Comparison picture** (kf_common.jpg): one row per rewritten keyframe - as painted, the version used for training and the amount of change (brighter = more change). With many keyframes only the 12 most rewritten are shown.
- **Full report** (kf_common.json): the figures of every keyframe.

## How to read it
The previews, the Loss and the keyframe MSE of the task page refer to the rewritten keyframes and cannot be compared directly with a task that has the setting off. The keyframe scores on the Experiments page refer to the keyframes as painted, so rewritten regions count as error there. Judge the effect on the in-between frames: whether the edit stays steady in playback.

metric_kfc_rewritten.title: Rewritten share
metric_kfc_rewritten.summary: The share of the keyframes' edited region that keyframe commonality noticeably rewrote, averaged over all keyframes.
metric_kfc_rewritten.body:
## How to read it
- A pixel counts as rewritten when its edit changes by about 5% or more; slighter adjustments are not counted. The edited region is where the Ground Truth differs from the input by about 3% or more.
- "N noticeably rewritten": the number of keyframes with a rewritten share above 0; "most": the keyframe with the highest share and that share.
- With consistent keyframes the share stays near 0%. A share concentrated on a few keyframes means those disagree with the others.

metric_kfc_common.title: Keyframe agreement
metric_kfc_common.summary: How far the other keyframes around each keyframe agree with each other inside its edited region, given for three scales: overall look, texture and fine detail.
metric_kfc_common.body:
## How to read it
100% = the other keyframes' edits coincide, 0% = nothing in common; averaged over all keyframes.
- **Overall look**: broad light and colour above about 10 px.
- **Texture**: structures of about 4–10 px such as cracks, pores and wound edges.
- **Fine detail**: the finest layer, below 4 px.

Only places where the other keyframes agree with each other are rewritten (see [[doc:metric_kfc_rewritten]]). On a scale with low agreement hardly anything is rewritten; differences between the keyframes on that scale cannot be corrected by this setting.

monitor_preview.title: Full-frame preview
monitor_preview.summary: Full-frame previews of the keyframes saved as training progresses: input, model output and Ground Truth side by side, browsable by step.
monitor_preview.body:
## What it does
- **Training Preview**: a full-frame comparison (Input | Output | Target) is saved at every [[doc:contact_sheet_interval]]; the slider and the play buttons browse through the steps.
- **Input / Ground Truth**: browse the keyframe inputs and Ground Truth images of the dataset.
- Images are displayed in sRGB (through OCIO); the data itself is linear ACEScg, see [[doc:color_pipeline]].
- Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, Reset Zoom to return.

## Limitations
Previews are rendered in the background; when the GPU is busy an occasional preview is skipped, training is not affected. With [[doc:preview_gpu]] set to off, no full-frame previews are produced.

monitor_preview_keyframe.title: Preview keyframe
monitor_preview_keyframe.summary: Selects which keyframe the full-frame preview shows.
monitor_preview_keyframe.body:
## What it does
Each keyframe has its own set of training previews; after switching, the preview shows that keyframe at every saved step.

monitor_playback.title: Playback controls
monitor_playback.summary: Steps through or plays the preview images: previous, play / pause, next, the slider, and FPS for the playback speed.
monitor_playback.body:
## What it does
The full-frame preview steps through the saved steps, the contact sheet through the Contact Sheet Interval images. FPS is the number of images shown per second (1–60) and affects the display only.

monitor_contact_sheet.title: Contact Sheet
monitor_contact_sheet.summary: Crop comparison during training: 3 rows of crops, each showing input, groundtruth and output, as in the Nuke CopyCat contact sheet.
monitor_contact_sheet.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
The same contact sheet image CopyCat writes, named `Training_YYMMDD_HHMMSS.<step>.png` in the task folder.

## What it does
One is saved at every [[doc:contact_sheet_interval]]. The 3 rows are crops of the current training batch at the current resolution stage; the labels show the stage and the Crop Size. Use it to check whether edges, grain and detail are being learned.

## How to read it
The closer output is to groundtruth, the better. Crops of the 1/4 and 1/2 stages have a lower resolution; judge detail at 1/1. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan.

monitor_cs_overlay.title: Show grid and labels
monitor_cs_overlay.summary: Overlays the 3×3 grid and the crop 1–3, input, groundtruth and output labels on the contact sheet. Display only.
monitor_cs_overlay.body:
## What it does
The labels match the Nuke CopyCat contact sheet. Turn it off to see the image without overlay.

monitor_cs_pixelated.title: Pixelated zoom
monitor_cs_pixelated.summary: Shows the original pixels when the contact sheet is zoomed in, without smoothing, for checking edges and grain pixel by pixel. Display only.
monitor_cs_pixelated.body:
## What it does
When off, the zoomed image is interpolated smoothly; it looks softer but hides differences between single pixels.

monitor_loss_chart.title: Loss curve
monitor_loss_chart.summary: The Loss over the training steps, plus the keyframe MSE at every checkpoint.
monitor_loss_chart.body:
## How to read it
- **Raw Loss** (light): every recorded value; **Smoothed Loss** (dark): an exponential moving average set by Smoothing.
- **Keyframe MSE** (green dots): the [[doc:metric_val_mse]] of each checkpoint.
- Vertical lines mark the resolution stage changes (1/4 → 1/2, 1/2 → 1/1); the Loss jumps there.
- A curve that flattens within a stage means further training gains less.

## Limitations
The Loss comes from random crops, so it fluctuates. Judge the result on the full-frame preview and the keyframe MSE.

monitor_loss_log.title: Log scale
monitor_loss_log.summary: Shows the vertical axis of the loss curve on a logarithmic scale, so that changes at low loss stay visible. Display only.
monitor_loss_log.body:
## What it does
Late in training the Loss is usually orders of magnitude lower than at the start; on a log scale the changes of every stage remain visible.

monitor_loss_smooth.title: Smoothing
monitor_loss_smooth.summary: How strongly the loss curve is smoothed, from 0 (none) to 0.95. Display only.
monitor_loss_smooth.body:
## What it does
The smoothed curve is an exponential moving average: higher values give a steadier curve that reacts more slowly. The raw Loss is always shown in a lighter colour.

monitor_quality.title: Training quality (in-between frames)
monitor_quality.summary: Measures, during training, what the model does on the in-between frames: edit strength, detail kept, drift over time and background change. There is no ground truth: use it to follow trends and find frames where the edit weakens.
monitor_quality.body:
## What it does
At checkpoints, the weights of that moment are run on the frames of the validation sequence from the first to the last keyframe and measured (evenly sampled above 96 frames). Measuring does not change the trained weights.

| Measure | Unit and reference | Ideal |
|---|---|---|
| [[doc:metric_kf_fit]] | dB (PSNR, peak = linear value 1.0) | higher = closer to the keyframes |
| [[doc:metric_q_strength]] | %, 100% = as strong as the keyframes on both sides | near 100% |
| [[doc:metric_q_detail]] / [[doc:metric_q_texture]] | %, 100% = as much as on the keyframes | near 100% |
| [[doc:metric_q_look_drift]] / [[doc:metric_q_tex_drift]] | change as % of itself | lower = steadier |
| [[doc:metric_q_bg]] | %, full white (linear 1.0) = 100% | near 0% |

## Requirements
RGB → RGB training; a dataset with a validation sequence whose frames include the keyframe inputs; in-between frames between the keyframes. Otherwise the card states the reason.

## How to read it
- The first measurement follows after about 2% of the total steps; later ones are taken at checkpoints, using no more than about 3% of the training time. The last step is always measured.
- These are reference measures without ground truth, not a score of the final picture; a high keyframe fit does not mean the in-between frames are good.
- In the 1/4 and 1/2 stages detail is naturally low and strength is still rising; judge the values of the 1/1 stage.
- The keyframe fit refers to the keyframes used for training (the rewritten ones when keyframe commonality is on).
- The card gives two hints only, and only in the 1/1 stage: the edit strength of a frame below 60%, or detail kept below 60%.

metric_kf_fit.title: Keyframe fit
metric_kf_fit.summary: PSNR (dB) of the model output against the keyframe Ground Truth, computed inside the edited region and over the whole frame. Higher means the keyframes are reproduced more accurately.
metric_kf_fit.body:
## How to read it
- **Edited region**: only pixels where the Ground Truth differs from the input (by more than 0.005 in linear value). When the edit covers a small part of the frame, this reflects the edit itself better than the whole-frame value. For an Alpha output, the region is the matte's foreground. When the region covers less than 0.05% or more than 90% of the frame, the whole-frame value is used.
- **Whole frame**: all pixels.
- PSNR is computed on linear ACEScg values with a peak of 1.0; about 3 dB higher halves the squared error.
- The two values of the checkpoint recommendation are this measure.

## Limitations
It measures the training keyframes only, not the in-between frames. With [[doc:adv_kf_common]] on, the checkpoint recommendation refers to the keyframes as painted.

metric_q_strength.title: In-between edit strength
metric_q_strength.summary: Strength of the edit on the in-between frames relative to the keyframes on either side: 100% means as strong, lower means the edit fades there.
metric_q_strength.body:
## How to read it
- **Mean**: the average over all in-between frames; **weakest**: the lowest frame and its frame number.
- Computed as the strength of the overall-look layer of the model's edit (output relative to the validation-sequence frame), divided by the strength painted on the keyframes on both sides (interpolated linearly in time).
- The weakest frame is usually far from a keyframe or where the picture changes most (head turns, expressions, occlusions); a keyframe near it helps most. Per-frame values: [[doc:monitor_quality_strip]].

metric_q_detail.title: Detail kept
metric_q_detail.summary: Detail kept inside the edited region of the in-between frames, relative to the detail painted on the keyframes: 100% means as much, lower means softer.
metric_q_detail.body:
## How to read it
- Covers all detail of the model's edit once its overall-look layer is removed, inside the region the model edits (pixels where the output differs from the validation-sequence frame by more than 0.005), averaged over all in-between frames.
- For structures of 3–10 px only, see [[doc:metric_q_texture]].
- Values are naturally low in the 1/4 and 1/2 stages; judge the 1/1 stage.

metric_q_texture.title: Texture
metric_q_texture.summary: Texture of about 3–10 px (cracks, pores, wound edges) inside the edited region of the in-between frames, relative to the keyframes: 100% means as much.
metric_q_texture.body:
## How to read it
Shown in the second line of Detail Kept. Computed like [[doc:metric_q_detail]], restricted to the 3–10 px band.

metric_q_look_drift.title: Overall-look drift
metric_q_look_drift.summary: How much the overall brightness and colour of the edit change when followed along the motion over several frames, as a percentage of itself. Lower is steadier.
metric_q_look_drift.body:
## How to read it
- The gap is 5 frames by default; when in-between frames are sampled, the actual gap is used and shown on the card.
- 0% = no change; pumping or swimming of the edit raises it.
- Computed by carrying the overall-look layer of the later frame onto the earlier one along the optical flow of the validation sequence and comparing them inside the region the model edits: the energy of the difference divided by the energy of the layer itself.

metric_q_tex_drift.title: Texture drift
metric_q_tex_drift.summary: How much the texture of the edit changes when followed along the motion for 1 and 5 frames ('boiling'), as a percentage of itself. Lower is steadier.
metric_q_tex_drift.body:
## How to read it
- The main value uses a 1-frame gap, the second line a 5-frame gap.
- **Plate floor**: the validation sequence's own texture measured the same way; even a perfect result shows this much change, so a value near the floor is steady.
- Computed like [[doc:metric_q_look_drift]], restricted to the 3–10 px texture band.

metric_q_bg.title: Background change
metric_q_bg.summary: Mean change of the pixels outside the edited region, as a percentage of full white (linear value 1.0). Should stay near 0%.
metric_q_bg.body:
## How to read it
The mean absolute difference between the output and the validation-sequence frame outside the region the model edits (pixels that differ by more than 0.005, grown by 8 px). It reflects subtle changes to the untouched area, such as grain being slightly smoothed; it should stay near 0%.

monitor_quality_chart.title: Training quality curves
monitor_quality_chart.summary: The training-quality measures over the training steps, on the same step axis as the loss curve.
monitor_quality_chart.body:
## How to read it
- Top: edit strength and detail kept (100% = as on the keyframes).
- Middle: overall-look drift and texture drift (lower = steadier); the dotted line is the plate floor of the texture drift.
- Bottom: keyframe fit (edited region, dB).
- The vertical axis is fixed at 0%–120%; larger values are drawn at the top edge and marked ▲. Hover or use the left and right arrow keys to read each measurement.

monitor_quality_strip.title: Edit strength per frame
monitor_quality_strip.summary: Edit strength of every in-between frame in the latest measurement, in validation-sequence frame order, with the keyframes and the weakest frame marked.
monitor_quality_strip.body:
## How to read it
Bar height is the edit strength of that frame (100% = as strong as the keyframes on both sides); diamonds mark the keyframes (not measured here); the brightest bar is the weakest frame. Stretches with persistently low strength are good places for an additional keyframe. Hover or use the left and right arrow keys to read single frames.

monitor_quality_table.title: Training quality table
monitor_quality_table.summary: Lists every measurement with all its values and the measuring time, plus the per-frame strength of the latest measurement.
monitor_quality_table.body:
## How to read it
One row per measurement, newest first. The columns are explained in the entries of the measures; Measuring time is the number of seconds the measurement took.

monitor_models.title: Model versions
monitor_models.summary: All model versions saved by this task, listed by step and downloadable one by one.
monitor_models.body:
## In Nuke CopyCat
The same model files CopyCat writes at every Checkpoint Interval, named `Training_YYMMDD_HHMMSS.<step>`.

## What it does
A version is saved automatically at every [[doc:checkpoint_interval]], on pause and at the end of training. The list shows step and Epoch, file name, the Loss at that step, the [[doc:metric_val_mse]], file size and time saved; the tags are explained in [[doc:monitor_model_tags]].

## How to read it
When the run finished its Epochs, the last version is usually the best. Tasks with a validation sequence can compute a [[doc:monitor_rec]].

monitor_model_file.title: Model file name
monitor_model_file.summary: Model files are named the way Nuke CopyCat names them: Training_date_time.step.
monitor_model_file.body:
## What it does
The prefix `Training_YYMMDD_HHMMSS` is the task's time stamp, the suffix the step, for example `Training_261116_093000.12000.pt`. The format is TorchScript (.pt).

## Requirements
In Nuke, convert the .pt file to .cat with the CatFileCreator node, then use it in the Inference node.

## How to read it
A version marked "Exported on download" in the Size / Saved At column has no file yet; it is exported when downloaded.

monitor_model_tags.title: Version tags
monitor_model_tags.summary: Tags in the model version list: latest, lowest keyframe MSE, and the Balanced and Detail picks of the checkpoint recommendation.
monitor_model_tags.body:
## How to read it
- **Latest**: the last saved version.
- **Lowest keyframe MSE**: the version with the lowest [[doc:metric_val_mse]].
- **Balanced**, **Detail**: see [[doc:monitor_rec_balanced]] and [[doc:monitor_rec_detail]]; versions with a recommendation tag also show the edited-region [[doc:metric_kf_fit]].
- **Lowest HFI (older tasks)**: appears only in recommendations saved by older tasks; HFI does not measure flicker, see [[doc:metric_hfi]].

monitor_rec.title: Checkpoint recommendation
monitor_rec.summary: Evaluates the saved checkpoints on the keyframes and the validation sequence and suggests two versions: Balanced (the latest full-resolution checkpoint) and Detail (best fit of the edited region).
monitor_rec.body:
## What it does
Compute Recommendation evaluates about 10 checkpoints (including those at the resolution stage changes and the last two); each is inferred on all keyframes and on up to 60 frames of the validation sequence. The two picks are then shown and tagged in the model version list. For tasks with auto-extend or early stop, the corresponding badge is shown as well (see [[doc:auto_extend]] and [[doc:lab_stop_after_best]]).

## Requirements
The dataset has a validation sequence and the task is not training.

## How to read it
- [[doc:monitor_rec_balanced]]: the default choice.
- [[doc:monitor_rec_detail]]: describes the fit of the keyframes' edited region only.
- The two values on each card are the edited-region and whole-frame [[doc:metric_kf_fit]].

monitor_rec_balanced.title: Balanced (recommended)
monitor_rec_balanced.summary: The latest full-resolution (1/1) checkpoint. When the run finished its Epochs, this is usually the best version.
monitor_rec_balanced.body:
## How to read it
For matte (Alpha) outputs, checkpoints whose foreground clearly collapsed are skipped (edit magnitude below 85% of the full-resolution reference).

## Limitations
When training is stopped midway, the last checkpoint is not necessarily the best. If you plan to stop early or to use a mid-run checkpoint, turn on [[doc:adv_ema]] to make mid-run checkpoints steadier.

monitor_rec_detail.title: Detail
monitor_rec_detail.summary: The full-resolution checkpoint that fits the edited region of the keyframes best (high edited-region PSNR, low edge error).
monitor_rec_detail.body:
## Limitations
It reflects the fit to the training keyframes only; the in-between frames are not necessarily better. When it differs from Balanced, compare the in-between frames of both versions in Nuke.

monitor_log.title: Training log
monitor_log.summary: Live output of the training process (train.log), including the full Python traceback when an error occurs.
monitor_log.body:
## What it does
Shows the latest log lines: the Loss and speed at every [[doc:log_interval]], the keyframe MSE at every checkpoint and what the advanced settings did. Auto-scroll keeps the newest line in view; Copy Log copies everything shown; Refresh reads the log again immediately.

method.title: Test method
method.summary: Each setting is compared pairwise with the Nuke CopyCat defaults on the same data and the same keyframes, one setting at a time, scored only on frames the model never trained on.
method.body:
## Comparison

- Baseline: the Nuke CopyCat defaults (4 px crop grid, plain MSE loss, no advanced settings).
- On datasets whose height is not a multiple of 4, the baseline uses the top-anchored 4 px grid, so that the training crops and full-frame inference share the same sampling phase; otherwise any setting that changes the crop grid would be credited with the effect of the phase misalignment. The phase effect itself is reported in [[ev:adv_crop_grid_anchor]].
- Single comparison = baseline plus one setting; combinations (scene presets) are also tested as "combination minus one setting".
- 3 seeds per configuration (1, 2, 3); results are mean ± seed standard deviation.
- Inference as in Nuke Inference: full frame, padded on the right and bottom to a multiple of 16, sampling grid anchored at the top-left corner.

## Scoring

- Scored only on unseen frames: they are never trained on and never used to choose a configuration, checkpoint or parameter.
- Only the final step counts; training curves are evaluated at 5 fixed points: 1/3, 1/2, 2/3 and 5/6 of the steps and the final step.
- Main metric: PSNR (dB, higher = closer to the ground truth) in linear ACEScg, peak 1.0, computed per frame and averaged over frames.
- Display PSNR: computed after conversion to sRGB and clipping to 0–1; more sensitive to errors in dark areas, insensitive to highlights.
- Mattes: IoU (threshold 0.5, higher is better) and SAD (in thousands of pixels, lower is better).
- Verdict: an absolute difference of the means below 0.5 dB, or not larger than the larger of the two seed standard deviations, counts as "no difference".

## Scale

- 6 datasets, one shot per task type (2 for roto), see [[ev:appendix_material]].
- Standard setting: Small, 5 keyframes, Crop 256, batch 5, 100k Epochs (100k steps), learning rate 1e-4 (poly 0.3), three-stage multi-resolution, mixed precision fixed to FP16.
- Additional comparisons of training length (30k and 300k Epochs), model size (Medium, Large) and number of keyframes (2–17); 310 training runs in total.

## Repeatability

The same configuration with the same seed, trained 7 times (different GPUs and repeated runs), has a standard deviation of 0.08 dB in unseen-frame PSNR (range 0.22 dB); between seeds the standard deviation is 0.19 dB. Differences below about 0.2 dB are not meaningful in this setup.

## Measurements beyond PSNR

- Unedited-area error: mean deviation of the output from the input on pixels where ground truth and input are identical.
- Overall-look drift: how much the large-scale brightness and colour of the edit layer change over 5 frames along the image motion, as a percentage of its own magnitude; lower is steadier.
- Detail energy: energy of the fine detail of the edit layer relative to the ground truth (100% = same as the ground truth, lower = softer).

## Other test sets

- Keyframe commonality and averaged weights on face shots use separate paired tests (same keyframes, same machine, on / off); the conditions are given in each entry.
- Some entries cite single-seed long-run records (up to 1M steps, 2 unseen frames per dataset). These data are used only for comparisons within the same run, or for several comparisons that agree in direction, and are marked as such.

appendix_material.title: Test material
appendix_material.summary: The tests use 6 general datasets and 4 face datasets, all from public footage; except for roto, the edits are synthetic or analytic, so every frame has a ground truth.
appendix_material.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

There is one shot per task type (2 for roto); on other footage the size of the effects can differ. Only the roto ground truth is hand-made; the other edits are more regular than real hand-made edits.

## Test conditions

- Keyframes are spread evenly over the clip; unseen frames are spread over the whole clip between the keyframes, in a fixed number.
- The defocus and degrain datasets have a ground truth on every 2nd frame (33 frames of the clip: 9 keyframe candidates, 24 unseen frames).
- A small dataset of 12 tiles of 256×256 is used only to check failure cases and is not part of any conclusion: 8 training tiles are too few, and the unprocessed input beats every trained model.

## Results

General datasets (Nuke defaults: Small, 5 keyframes, 100k Epochs, phase-aligned, 3 seeds):

| Dataset | Footage and ground truth | Resolution (px) | H mod 4 | Channels | Unseen frames | No-processing PSNR (dB) | Nuke defaults PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Green-screen keying | Foundry sample green-screen footage; ground truth from an analytic keyer | 960×540 | 0 | 3→4 | 43 | 7.15 | 59.00 ± 0.19 |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | Foundry SmartVector sample footage; decals and markers synthetic | 960×540 | 0 | 3→3 | 48 | 30.20 | 51.80 ± 0.10 |
| Defocus | Tears of Steel 01_2a; disc blur (radius 4.6 px) synthetic | 960×506 | 2 | 3→3 | 24 | 24.14 | 36.29 ± 0.19 |
| Degrain | Tears of Steel 01_1a; grain synthetic | 960×506 | 2 | 3→3 | 24 | 34.49 | 40.85 ± 0.09 |
| Roto (parkour) | DAVIS-2017 parkour; hand-made mattes | 854×480 | 0 | 3→1 | 83 | — | 24.70 ± 0.26 (IoU 0.867) |
| Roto (dance) | DAVIS-2017 dance-twirl; hand-made mattes | 854×480 | 0 | 3→1 | 73 | — | 18.00 ± 0.24 (IoU 0.714) |

Face datasets (Tears of Steel live-action footage, synthetic edits, 3→3):

| Dataset | Shot | Resolution (px) | Keyframes | Unseen frames | No-processing PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Face ageing A | 05_3a | 700×700 | 6 | 41 | 35.51 |
| Wound paste A | 05_3a | 700×700 | 6 | 41 | 32.31 |
| Face ageing B | 05_1b | 860×860 | 11 | 89 | 37.30 |
| Wound paste B | 05_1b | 860×860 | 11 | 89 | 36.40 |
| Skin retouch A | 05_3a | 700×700 | 5 | 42 | 52.63 |
| Wound removal A | 05_3a | 700×700 | 5 | 42 | 46.20 |

## Limitations

Synthetic or analytic edits are more regular than real hand-made edits; on real production shots the size of the effects can differ.

adv_crop_grid.title: Crop grid: 1 px
adv_crop_grid.summary: The 1 px crop grid raised unseen-frame PSNR on keying, clean-up, defocus and degrain shots, by more the longer the training, at unchanged training speed; on roto mattes it made no difference.
adv_crop_grid.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Helps: keying, clean-up, defocus, degrain, and any shot whose height is not a multiple of 4 (see [[ev:adv_crop_grid_anchor]]).
- No difference: roto mattes (no difference in PSNR or IoU on the two test shots).

## Test conditions

Main test set ([[ev:method]]): Small, 5 keyframes, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds, compared with the phase-aligned Nuke defaults (4 px grid). The training-length comparison uses the clean-up dataset, each length trained separately.

## Results

| Dataset | 1 px: Δ PSNR (dB) | 1 px: Δ display PSNR (dB) | 2 px: Δ PSNR (dB) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Green-screen keying | +0.79 | +0.04 | +0.66 | 1 px better |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | +3.71 | +2.01 | +2.78 | 1 px better; 2 px 0.92 below 1 px |
| Defocus | +0.69 | +0.43 | +0.64 | 1 px better |
| Degrain | +0.86 | +0.66 | +0.74 | 1 px better |
| Roto (parkour) | +0.24 (IoU 0.871) | — | — | no difference |
| Roto (dance) | −0.18 (IoU 0.698) | — | — | no difference |

Training length (clean-up, 1 px relative to the 4 px baseline of the same length):

| Epochs | Δ PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|
| 30k | +1.14 |
| 100k | +3.71 |
| 300k | +5.61 |
| 1M (long-run record, single seed, 2 unseen frames) | +4.93 |

- On the 4 datasets that improved, all 3 seeds with 1 px are above all seeds of the baseline.
- 1 px lowers the training-frame PSNR (clean-up −1.92 dB, degrain −0.83, keying −0.40, roto parkour −6.31) while raising the unseen-frame PSNR: the model memorises the keyframes less and learns a position-independent mapping.
- On the defocus dataset (height 506), 1 px is +3.50 dB above the default bottom-anchored grid, most of it from the phase alignment (see [[ev:adv_crop_grid_anchor]]).
- Speed: 1 px runs at 99%–100% of the default path (RTX 4090 / 5090, Small / Medium / Large).

## Limitations

- One shot per task type; 4 of the datasets have synthetic edits.
- The 2 px grid is not included: on 4 datasets it is nowhere better than 1 px, at the same speed; on odd plate heights the bottom-anchored 2 px grid cannot reach the sampling phase of full-frame inference.

adv_crop_grid_anchor.title: Plate height and sampling phase (grid anchor)
adv_crop_grid_anchor.summary: When the plate height is not a multiple of 4, the default bottom-anchored 4 px grid is out of phase with full-frame inference: training-frame accuracy always drops, and unseen frames drop clearly on nearly static shots; the 1 px grid or the top anchor avoids it.
adv_crop_grid_anchor.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Only plates whose height is not a multiple of 4 are affected (for example 2048×858, 772×855); the width does not matter.
- The loss on unseen frames depends on the content: clear on nearly static shots, small when the content moves or changes every frame (grain).

## Test conditions

- The datasets of the main test set whose height is not a multiple of 4 (defocus, degrain, height 506), and the clean-up dataset cropped from the top to heights 537 / 538 / 539; Small, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds.
- Check in Nuke 17: a 7-frame 772×855 live-action EXR shot, trained with CopyCat, training frames rendered with the Inference node; measured inside a 16 px border.

## Results

Default bottom-anchored grid relative to the top-anchored grid:

| Dataset | H mod 4 | Δ training-frame PSNR (dB) | Δ unseen-frame PSNR (dB) | Verdict (unseen) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Defocus (506 rows) | 2 | −3.97 | −2.81 | lower |
| Degrain (506 rows) | 2 | −2.35 | +0.02 | no difference |
| Clean-up (cropped to 538 rows) | 2 | −6.77 | −0.35 | no difference |

- Clean-up cropped to 537 / 539 rows (H mod 4 = 1 / 3): unseen frames −0.43 / −0.05 dB relative to the original height, no difference.
- A model already trained with the default grid is realigned by cropping H mod 4 rows from the top before inference: the unseen-frame PSNR of defocus goes from 33.48 back to 36.45 dB.

Nuke 17 (training-frame PSNR):

| Training | Rendered as is (dB) | Top H mod 4 rows cropped before inference (dB) |
|---|---|---|
| Medium, 350k steps, height 855 | 38.86 | 49.15 |
| Small, 52.5k steps, height 855 | 37.28 | 40.94 |
| Small, 52.5k steps, height 856 (H mod 4 = 0) | 40.83 | 37.48 (1 row cropped, deliberately misaligned) |

## Limitations

- The effect on unseen frames was measured on 3 datasets.
- The default behaviour is the same as CopyCat (bottom anchor); the 1 px grid or the top anchor has to be selected manually.

adv_loss_grad.title: Gradient term
adv_loss_grad.summary: The gradient term clearly raises accuracy on keying (weight 0.15); on clean-up, 0.05 mainly raises the display PSNR; on degrain and defocus it has no measurable effect.
adv_loss_grad.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Helps: keying (0.15).
- Optional for clean-up at 0.05: the gain in linear PSNR disappears with longer training, the display PSNR stays higher.
- No measurable effect: degrain, defocus. Roto was not tested on its own.

## Test conditions

Main test set, Small, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds. "Alone" = phase-aligned 4 px baseline plus the gradient term; "with 1 px" = 1 px grid plus the gradient term, compared with the 1 px grid alone.

## Results

| Dataset | Weight | Alone: Δ PSNR (dB) | Alone: Δ display PSNR (dB) | With 1 px, relative to 1 px alone: Δ PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Green-screen keying | 0.15 | +2.13 | +9.02 | +3.79 |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | 0.05 | −0.37 | +0.84 | +0.56 |
| Defocus | 0.10 | −0.42 | −0.20 | — |
| Degrain | 0.05 | +0.41 | +0.27 | +0.29 |

- Clean-up, "1 px + gradient 0.05" relative to 1 px alone: at 300k Epochs the linear PSNR is −0.03 dB (no difference); the display PSNR is +2.56 dB at 100k and +0.98 dB at 300k.
- Removing the gradient term from the defocus combination (Small: 1 px + 15 / 25 / 60 + Charbonnier 0.25 + highlight damping 0.5): +0.24 dB, no difference.
- The full result of the keying combination is in [[ev:preset_keying_despill]].

## Limitations

One shot per task type; only the weights in the table were tested; Small only.

adv_loss_charbonnier.title: Charbonnier
adv_loss_charbonnier.summary: On the main test set (Small), Charbonnier raised linear PSNR nowhere and lowered it on keying and clean-up; on defocus it raises the display PSNR and stays in the defocus preset. On a live-action face shot with visible noise (Wound paste A, small edit) it reduces the changes in the unedited area to about 23% of those without it, linear PSNR unchanged, display PSNR 1.0 dB higher; with the settings of the face edit preset (Medium) it also raises the PSNR of unseen frames (except when the keyframes differ strongly from one another), so 0.25 is part of the face edit preset.
adv_loss_charbonnier.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Helps: the face edit preset (0.25, no gradient term and no highlight damping); the test on Medium is in [[ev:preset_face_edit]].
- Helps: defocus, together with the gradient term and highlight damping (see [[ev:preset_bokeh_focus]]).
- Helps: live-action plates with visible noise or grain where only part of the image is edited (for example a face wound) and the unedited area should stay as it is (0.25).
- Does not help: keying and clean-up on clean plates; degrain. Roto was not tested on its own.

## Test conditions

Main test set, Small, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds. "Alone" = phase-aligned 4 px baseline plus Charbonnier (0.30 for keying, 0.25 otherwise); "removed" = only this term taken out of a combination that contains it.

Face shots: Wound paste A and Face ageing B ([[ev:appendix_material]]; this test uses 5 keyframes each, 42 / 95 unseen frames), Small, 100k steps, 1 px grid, 3 seeds; "1 px + Charbonnier 0.25" against "1 px only".

## Results

| Dataset | Comparison | Δ PSNR (dB) | Δ display PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Green-screen keying | alone (0.30) | −1.15 | +2.96 |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | alone (0.25) | −0.79 | −0.20 |
| Defocus | alone (0.25) | +0.31 | +0.74 |
| Degrain | alone (0.25) | −0.04 | −0.09 |
| Green-screen keying | removed from "1 px + Charbonnier 0.30 + gradient 0.15 + highlight damping 0.35" | +3.16 | +3.27 |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | removed from "1 px + Charbonnier 0.25 + gradient 0.05 + highlight damping 0.5" | +1.01 | +1.08 |
| Defocus | removed from the defocus combination (Small) | −0.34 | −0.60 |
| Wound paste A | added to 1 px (0.25) | +0.47 | +1.02 |
| Face ageing B | added to 1 px (0.25) | +0.23 | +0.44 |

- Linear PSNR improves nowhere; on defocus the gain in display PSNR (alone +0.74, removed −0.60) passes the threshold.
- Wound paste A: unedited-area error ([[ev:method]]) 3.5e-04 → 8.1e-05 (×0.23, per seed ×0.21–×0.27); PSNR of the edited area (pixels where truth and input differ) +0.29 dB (no effect). The plate's high-frequency variation in flat areas is about 5.5 times that of the clean-up dataset.
- Face ageing B (84% of the pixels edited, same plate noise as Wound paste A): linear +0.23, display +0.44, edited area +0.10 dB (all no effect), unedited-area error ×0.71 - no harm with a large edit.

## Limitations

The face results of this entry are on Small, with two noisy live-action face shots only (Wound paste A, Face ageing B); the test of the face edit preset (Medium) on 5 face shots is in [[ev:preset_face_edit]].

adv_loss_hdr.title: Highlight damping (HDR α)
adv_loss_hdr.summary: Highlight damping had no measurable effect on linear PSNR in 7 comparisons; it slightly raises the display PSNR on clean-up and defocus, and is kept only in the defocus preset together with the other two loss terms.
adv_loss_hdr.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Not recommended on its own; used in the defocus preset together with Charbonnier and the gradient term (see [[ev:preset_bokeh_focus]]).
- With a single-channel matte output, highlight damping is fixed at 0.

## Test conditions

Main test set, Small, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds. "Alone" = phase-aligned 4 px baseline plus highlight damping (0.35 for keying, 0.5 otherwise); "removed" = only highlight damping taken out of a combination.

## Results

| Dataset | Comparison | Δ PSNR (dB) | Δ display PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Green-screen keying | alone (0.35) | −0.16 | +0.07 |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | alone (0.5) | +0.09 | +0.57 |
| Defocus | alone (0.5) | +0.44 | +0.51 |
| Degrain | alone (0.5) | 0.00 | −0.04 |
| Green-screen keying | removed from "1 px + Charbonnier 0.30 + gradient 0.15 + highlight damping 0.35" | −0.21 | −0.06 |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | removed from "1 px + Charbonnier 0.25 + gradient 0.05 + highlight damping 0.5" | −0.04 | −0.32 |
| Defocus | removed from the defocus combination (Small) | +0.20 | −0.05 |

- All 7 comparisons are within the threshold in linear PSNR (−0.21 to +0.44 dB).

## Limitations

Not separated from the other two loss terms on Large.

adv_stages.title: Stage ratios 15 / 25 / 60
adv_stages.summary: Giving 60% of the steps to the full-resolution stage (15 / 25 / 60, 200 transition steps) raised unseen-frame accuracy on defocus, at about 27% longer training; on other tasks it was not tested with several seeds.
adv_stages.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Helps: defocus. On that dataset the unseen-frame PSNR is still at the no-processing level at the end of the 1/4 and 1/2 stages (see [[ev:appendix_material]]); all of the gain happens in the 1/1 stage, so giving that stage more steps pays off.
- Keying, clean-up and degrain learn most of their result in the low-resolution stages; keep equal thirds for them.

## Test conditions

Defocus dataset of the main test set, Small, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds; warm-up (transition) 200 steps.

## Results

| Comparison | Δ PSNR (dB) | Δ display PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|
| Alone: phase-aligned baseline + 15 / 25 / 60 | +1.01 | +0.87 |
| Removed from the defocus combination (Small) | −1.53 | −1.28 |

Defocus, phase-aligned baseline, unseen-frame PSNR during training (mean of 3 seeds):

| Point | 1/3 (end of the 1/4 stage) | 2/3 (end of the 1/2 stage) | 5/6 |
|---|---|---|---|
| PSNR (dB) | 24.04 | 23.83 | 35.08 |

| Model | Training speed of the whole run (relative to equal thirds, %) |
|---|---|
| Small | 73–75 |
| Medium | 71–73 |
| Large | 71–73 |

- Long-run records (single seed, 500k steps, 2 unseen frames): defocus Medium +0.77 dB; keying Medium −0.69 dB.

## Limitations

Tested with several seeds on one defocus shot only; other ratios (for example 45 / 40 / 15) were not tested.

adv_ema.title: Averaged weights (EMA)
adv_ema.summary: Averaged weights do not change a model trained to the end; at checkpoints from the middle of a run they are mostly better on keying, clean-up and face shots, and make no difference on defocus, degrain and roto.
adv_ema.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Helps: when training is stopped early or a checkpoint from the middle of the run is used; clearest on keying, clean-up and face shots.
- No effect: on a run trained to the end (final step); on defocus, degrain and roto.

## Test conditions

- Pairs within the same run: at every checkpoint the current weights and the averaged weights (β 0.9995, restarted at every resolution stage) are evaluated together. Both come from the same training trajectory and are not affected by seeds or phase.
- Main test set: clean-up and degrain, Small, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds.
- Long-run records: single seed, up to 1M steps, 2 unseen frames per dataset; averaging with β 0.9995 (in these records it does not restart per stage, see the averaging-window line in the results). Final step: 170 runs; middle of the run: the 1,080 checkpoints between 20% and 99% of the training in 172 runs.
- Face shots: wound paste B and face ageing B ([[ev:appendix_material]]), 7 runs (consistent keyframes and simulated inconsistent keyframes, 1 of them with keyframe commonality), Small, 100k steps, 1 px grid, L1 loss, evaluated at 10 points of the training.

## Results

Final step (averaged weights − current weights):

| Test | Runs | Δ PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|
| Main test set | 6 | −0.05 to +0.01 |
| Long-run records | 170 | mean −0.004 (−0.18 to +0.12) |
| Face shots | 7 | −0.14 to +0.05 |

Middle of the run (long-run records, 20%–99% of the training):

| Task | Checkpoints | Mean Δ PSNR (dB) | Share more than 0.5 dB better (%) | Largest Δ (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keying | 100 | +0.28 | 19 | +4.26 |
| Clean-up | 56 | +0.22 | 12 | +2.21 |
| Defocus | 88 | +0.01 | 0 | +0.19 |
| Degrain | 56 | +0.02 | 0 | +0.09 |
| Roto | 180 | −0.03 | 1 | +0.84 |

- Keying and clean-up by model size: Small +0.32, Medium +0.25, Large +0.16 dB.
- Main test set, clean-up: at 5/6 of the steps +2.14 / +0.47 / +0.09 dB (3 seeds), at 1/2 +0.45 / +0.87 / +0.24 dB; degrain within ±0.13 dB.
- Face shots: 10%–30% of the training mean +0.04 dB (67% of the checkpoints better); 40%–60% mean +0.20 dB (76%); 70%–90% mean +0.29 dB (90%), largest +1.00 dB.
- Averaging window: a β 0.9999 average that is not restarted at stage changes is behind the per-stage restarted average 33k steps after the 1/2 → 1/1 change (defocus mean −1.49 dB, up to −5.27; keying −0.57; clean-up −0.27); with β 0.9995 no restart is needed at that point.
- Speed: 98%–99% of the default path.

## Limitations

The long-run records are single-seed with 2 unseen frames per dataset; only 2 face shots.

adv_augment_flip.title: Horizontal flip
adv_augment_flip.summary: Horizontal flip improved accuracy consistently in no test: alone on clean-up the gain stays below the threshold, combined it lowers accuracy, and it lowers both face shots (Wound paste A by 1.7 dB, Face ageing B by 0.5 dB). It is in no preset.
adv_augment_flip.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- No consistent improvement was measured.
- Face shots: keep it off.
- With text, asymmetric logos or one-directional motion in the image, flipped samples do not match the real picture; keep it off.

## Test conditions

Clean-up dataset, Small, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds, flip probability 0.5.

Face shots: Wound paste A (this test uses 5 keyframes and 42 unseen frames) and Face ageing B (5 keyframes, 95 unseen frames), Small, 100k steps, 1 px grid, 3 seeds, flip probability 0.5; "1 px + flip" against "1 px only".

## Results

| Comparison | Δ PSNR (dB) | Δ display PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|
| Alone: phase-aligned baseline + flip | +0.48 | +0.10 |
| Added to "1 px + Charbonnier 0.25 + gradient 0.05 + highlight damping 0.5" | −0.70 | −0.38 |
| Wound paste A: added to 1 px | −1.73 | −1.54 |
| Face ageing B: added to 1 px | −0.53 | −0.58 |

- Alone, the 3 seeds agree in direction but stay below the 0.5 dB threshold; the two comparisons point in opposite directions.
- Wound paste A: lower with every seed (−1.75 / −1.70 / −1.74 dB); edited-area PSNR −1.77 dB, unedited-area error ×1.05; Face ageing B: lower with every seed (−0.56 / −0.49 / −0.55 dB).
- Speed: 96%–99% of the default path.

## Limitations

The clean-up dataset and two face shots.

adv_kf_common.title: Keyframe commonality
adv_kf_common.summary: When single keyframes disagree locally, keyframe commonality clearly raises unseen-frame accuracy; when all keyframes differ slightly, it lowers the frame-to-frame drift of the overall look; consistent keyframes give the same result as without it.
adv_kf_common.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Helps: one region of a single keyframe painted weaker, stronger, shifted or with redrawn texture while the other keyframes agree; overall brightness or colour that differs slightly from keyframe to keyframe.
- Unchanged: keyframes that already agree.
- Cannot fix: detail that every keyframe repainted differently, with nothing in common (detail energy drops in the "all slightly different" row).

## Test conditions

- 4 public face test shots ([[ev:appendix_material]]), 6 or 11 keyframes, 41 or 89 unseen frames, consistent synthetic ground truth.
- The inconsistent keyframes are simulated. Local outlier: on about half of the keyframes one region of the edit (radius 6%–11% of the shorter image side) is painted down to 25%, up to 200%, shifted by 5–9 px or has its texture redrawn. All slightly different: every keyframe has random differences in placement, medium-scale structure, detail and strength, scaled to the statistics of real artist keyframes.
- Paired training: same keyframes, same machine, on / off; Small (also Medium), 100k steps, 1 px grid, L1 loss, training seed 1; DIS optical flow, module at the product defaults.
- Unseen-frame PSNR against the consistent ground truth; overall-look drift and detail energy as defined in [[ev:method]].

## Results

| Keyframes | Model | Pairs | Off → on (dB, mean) | Δ PSNR (dB, mean, min to max) | Overall-look drift (over 5 frames, %) | Detail energy (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Consistent | Small | 4 | 51.69 → 51.70 | +0.01 (−0.01 to +0.03) | 0.9 → 0.7 | 94 → 94 |
| Consistent | Medium | 4 | 53.48 → 53.44 | −0.05 (−0.15 to +0.02) | 0.9 → 0.7 | 97 → 96 |
| Local outlier | Small | 6 | 49.34 → 51.13 | +1.79 (+0.78 to +2.64) | 1.9 → 0.7 | 92 → 92 |
| Local outlier | Medium | 6 | 50.85 → 52.82 | +1.97 (+1.14 to +2.89) | 2.1 → 0.7 | 94 → 94 |
| Local outlier, 300k steps | Small | 1 | 50.34 → 52.92 | +2.58 | 2.0 → 0.8 | 90 → 90 |
| All slightly different | Small | 4 | 37.99 → 38.85 | +0.87 (+0.20 to +1.60) | 18.9 → 8.1 | 79 → 73 |

- For reference, the overall-look drift of the consistent ground truth itself is 0.2%–3.4%.
- With local outliers the detail energy is unchanged: the correction happens only where a keyframe disagrees, nothing is averaged.

## Limitations

- Single training seed; the keyframe inconsistencies are simulated; 1–6 pairs per case.
- Trained with an L1 loss.
- Regions where the optical flow cannot follow fast motion are left as they are; with fast motion the default optical flow can slightly change keyframes that agree (worst consistent pair −0.15 dB).

model_size.title: Model Size
model_size.summary: There is no single best model size: Large is clearly better for defocus, Medium better for clean-up and face shots, for keying Medium equals Small at 100k, and Small is about 2.0 dB better at 300k, and degrain and roto mattes get worse with larger models.
model_size.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Large: defocus.
- Medium: clean-up, face shots (about 1.5 times the training time of Small; the full clean-up settings see [[ev:preset_cleanup_grain]], face shots see [[ev:preset_face_edit]]).
- Small: keying (no difference from Medium at 100k, Small better with longer training), degrain, roto mattes.

## Test conditions

Main test set, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds. Keying also compared at 300k Epochs (1 px + gradient 0.15). Keying, clean-up and degrain compared on the 1 px grid; roto on the default grid; defocus with the phase-aligned baseline and with the defocus preset. Δ relative to Small with the same setting.

## Results

| Dataset | Setting | Medium: Δ PSNR (dB) | Large: Δ PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Green-screen keying | 1 px | −0.21 | — |
| Green-screen keying | 1 px + gradient 0.15, 300k Epochs | −1.97 | — |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | 1 px | +1.11 | — |
| Defocus | phase-aligned baseline | +2.03 | +2.91 |
| Defocus | 1 px + 15 / 25 / 60 | — | +4.17 |
| Defocus | defocus preset | — | +4.42 |
| Degrain | 1 px | −0.44 | −0.85 |
| Roto (parkour) | default | −1.52 (IoU 0.803) | −3.96 (IoU 0.670) |

- Larger models reach a higher training-frame PSNR (roto parkour Small → Large +9.70 dB) but a lower unseen-frame PSNR: they memorise the keyframes more.
- Training time: Medium about 1.5–1.6 times Small, Large about 3.5–3.9 times (RTX 4090 / 5090, batch 8, Crop 256).
- Green-screen keying at 300k Epochs: Medium 63.68 vs Small 65.65 ± 0.32 dB; alpha PSNR −1.90 dB, SAD 42% higher; Medium is lower at all 5 evaluation points (−1.97 to −3.58 dB) but higher on the training frames (69.01 vs 68.36 dB). Only the display PSNR is higher for Medium (+0.73 dB).
- Long-run records (single seed, 1M steps, 1 px + composite loss, 2 unseen frames): keying Medium and Large 2.25 / 1.49 dB below Small.
- Clean-up long-run records (single seed, 1M steps, 2 unseen frames): Medium equals Small (1 px + composite loss −0.05 dB, 4 px +0.04 dB) - the Medium advantage at 100k may not last in very long training, but Medium is not worse.

## Limitations

Large was not tested on keying and clean-up; one shot per task type; face shots see [[ev:preset_face_edit]].

crop_size.title: Crop Size
crop_size.summary: With a Crop Size close to the plate height, unseen-frame accuracy drops clearly and training becomes much slower; in multi-seed tests Crop 384 (71% of the plate height) equals Crop 256 (at more than twice the work per step).
crop_size.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

Keep Crop 256, or clearly below the plate height; do not go close to the plate height.

## Test conditions

Long-run records: single seed, 1M steps, 2 unseen frames per dataset; 1 px grid + composite loss (Charbonnier 0.25 + gradient 0.05 + highlight damping 0.5); same model and settings, only the Crop Size changed.

Main test set: green-screen keying, Small, 100k Epochs, 1 px grid only, Crop 384 (71% of the plate height) against Crop 256, 3 seeds.

## Results

| Dataset (plate height, px) | Model | Crop Size (px) | Δ PSNR relative to Crop 256 (dB) | Training time (relative to Crop 256) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Defocus (506) | Medium | 496 | −1.30 | ×2.22 |
| Defocus (506) | Large | 496 | −2.13 | ×1.86 |
| Green-screen keying (540) | Medium | 512 | −1.61 | ×3.36 |
| Green-screen keying (540) | Large | 512 | −2.57 | ×2.33 |

- All 4 comparisons agree in direction, each by more than the difference between repeated runs of the same configuration.
- Main test set, green-screen keying Crop 384: 59.56 vs 59.79 ± 0.10 dB with Crop 256 (−0.23, no effect); display +0.20, alpha −0.31 dB.

## Limitations

Long-run records: single seed, 2 unseen frames; of the sizes in between only Crop 384 on keying was tested.

epochs.title: Training length (Epochs)
epochs.summary: The right training length depends on the task: keying and clean-up still improve clearly from 100k to 300k Epochs, degrain stops improving after about 100k.
epochs.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Keying, clean-up (with the 1 px grid): the longer, the better.
- Degrain: about 100k Epochs is enough; longer brings nothing and gets worse without the 1 px grid.

## Test conditions

Main test set, Small, 5 keyframes, 3 seeds; every length trained separately, the learning rate decaying over its own total number of steps. In this test the batch equals the number of keyframes (5), so Epochs equal steps.

## Results

Change of the unseen-frame PSNR relative to the same setting at 100k Epochs (dB):

| Dataset | Setting | 30k (dB) | 300k (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Green-screen keying | Nuke defaults | — | +2.68 |
| Green-screen keying | 1 px + gradient 0.15 | — | +2.07 |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | Nuke defaults | −2.23 | +0.33 |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | 1 px | −4.80 | +2.22 |
| Tracking marker / stain removal | 1 px + gradient 0.05 | — | +1.63 |
| Degrain | Nuke defaults (phase-aligned) | +0.50 | −0.56 |
| Degrain | 1 px | −0.39 | −0.17 |

- Degrain at 300k: all 3 seeds with 1 px are below all seeds at 100k.
- Long-run records (single seed, 1M steps): all 8 degrain runs drop from the first checkpoint of the 1/1 stage to the final step (0.06–0.55 dB; 1 px grid 0.26–0.33 dB). With the 1 px grid, 17 keying, clean-up and defocus runs are still improving at 1M steps, and the final step is the best checkpoint of the 1/1 stage.

## Limitations

Multi-seed tests go up to 300k Epochs; defocus and roto were tested at 100k only.

dataset_keyframes.title: Number of keyframes
dataset_keyframes.summary: Keying and roto mattes are very sensitive to the number of keyframes and keep improving from 2 to 17; degrain is hardly sensitive; roto quality drops quickly with the distance to the nearest keyframe.
dataset_keyframes.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Roto: keyframes must be dense, no frame far from the nearest keyframe; fast limb motion needs a keyframe every few frames.
- Keying: the more keyframes, the better.
- Degrain: the number of keyframes has little effect.

## Test conditions

Main test set, nested keyframe sets (2 = first and last, 3 = plus the middle one, each further step adds one keyframe between every two neighbours), fixed unseen frames, 100k Epochs for all, 3 seeds; keying and degrain on the 1 px grid, roto on the default grid.

## Results

| Dataset | 2 keyframes | 3 keyframes | 9 keyframes | 17 keyframes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Green-screen keying: Δ PSNR relative to 5 (dB) | −5.78 | −1.77 | +1.50 | +4.92 |
| Degrain: Δ PSNR relative to 5 (dB) | −0.41 | −0.18 | +0.23 | — |
| Roto (parkour): IoU | 0.528 | 0.765 | 0.928 | 0.956 |

- Roto (dance, 5 keyframes): IoU drops with the distance to the nearest keyframe: 1–2 frames 0.918, 3–5 frames 0.778, 6–10 frames 0.587. Keying, clean-up, defocus and degrain hardly change with the distance (groups within the same keyframe count differ by less than 0.9 dB).
- With the same Epochs, 9 / 17 keyframes give 1.125 / 2.125 times the steps of 5 keyframes (batch capped at 8), so part of the gain comes from more training steps.

## Limitations

The number of keyframes was not tested on clean-up and defocus; keyframes were evenly spaced, the choice of keyframe positions was not tested; number of keyframes and number of steps are not separated.

speed_options.title: Speed options and training speed
speed_options.summary: The speed options do not change what is computed: the training loss matches Nuke CopyCat stage by stage, and on the same GPU a whole training run is about 1.8–5.5 times faster than CopyCat.
speed_options.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

All on by default; they change only how the work is executed (whole-step CUDA Graph, fused Adam, NHWC layout, cuDNN algorithm search, dataset resident in GPU memory, asynchronous saving). The low-resolution stages gain the most.

## Test conditions

- Equivalence: a 7-frame 772×855 live-action EXR shot, Medium, batch 4, 200k Epochs (350k steps), multi-resolution, seed 0; the same data and settings trained in Nuke 17 CopyCat and in WildCat.
- Speed: the same workstation and GPU, Nuke 17.0v2 CopyCat and WildCat at their defaults, multi-resolution on, Mixed Precision = Adaptive, steady-state steps/s per stage.

## Results

Training loss (window mean of the finest level):

| Step range | CopyCat | WildCat |
|---|---|---|
| 1k–117k (1/4) | 0.000339 | 0.000330 |
| 117k–233k (1/2) | 0.000133 | 0.000141 |
| 233k–300k (1/1) | 0.000093 | 0.000097 |
| 340k–350k | 0.000045 | 0.000046 |

- Both models rendered with Nuke Inference on a 113-frame sequence that was not trained on: the MSE between the two outputs is 0.000127 (for reference, the CopyCat output differs from its input by 0.001616).

Speed (RTX 5090, batch 4, Crop 256, 7 frames, 6000 steps):

| Model | Speed-up per stage (1/4 · 1/2 · 1/1) | Whole run |
|---|---|---|
| Small | ×8.5 · ×6.5 · ×3.8 | ×5.5 |
| Medium | ×8.5 · ×5.6 · ×3.1 | ×4.7 |
| Large | ×6.7 · ×4.5 · ×3.2 | ×4.1 |
