- The 14 settings on the Hardware Benchmarks page (RTX 4090 / 5090, Small / Medium / Large, batch 4 / 8, Crop 256 / 512): whole run ×1.8–×5.3, 1/4 stage ×3.2–×8.7.
- Running 2 or 3 trainings on the same GPU at once is not faster (RTX 5090, Small, batch 5: one training 280 steps/s, 2 together 268, 3 together 263), so each GPU runs one training at a time.

## Limitations

Equivalence was tested on one shot and one model size; training is not bit-reproducible (repeated runs with the same seed differ by about 0.07 dB); the speed-up depends on batch, Crop Size and GPU.

monitor_rec.title: Checkpoint recommendation
monitor_rec.summary: After a run has completed its Epochs, the last full-resolution checkpoint is the best evaluated checkpoint or close to it; the Balanced recommendation therefore takes the last qualified full-resolution checkpoint.
monitor_rec.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Applies to runs that completed their Epochs.
- Runs stopped early and checkpoints from the middle of a run: averaged weights make them steadier, see [[ev:adv_ema]].

## Test conditions

258 runs of the main test set, each evaluated on the unseen frames at 1/3, 1/2, 2/3 and 5/6 of the steps and at the final step; the recommendation rules were replayed on these records.

## Results

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Runs whose final step is the best of the 5 evaluation points (%) | 76.7 |
| Mean shortfall of the final step against the best step (dB) | 0.038 |
| Largest shortfall of the final step against the best step (dB; without the failure-case dataset, which reaches 0.67) | 0.36 |

- Per dataset (mean of 3 seeds): keying, clean-up and defocus are still improving after 5/6; degrain on the 4 px grid ends 0.20 dB below its best step, with 1 px 0.00; roto within 0.21 dB.
- Runs of 300k Epochs: on keying and clean-up the final step is the best step; on degrain the final step is 0.10 dB (1 px) and 0.22 dB (4 px) below the 5/6 point.
- The Detail recommendation (best fit of the edited region of the keyframes) equals the final step in 98.8% of the runs; in the other 3 it is at most 0.27 dB better on unseen frames.
- Rules not used (measured): choosing by the combined score without a validation sequence picks the final step in only 66.7% of the runs, unseen frames 0.50 dB lower on average and up to 5.13 dB; capping at a saturated keyframe PSNR (46 / 58 dB) fires in 83 / 258 runs, which are 1.56 dB lower on average.

## Limitations

The rules were replayed on records, there is no end-to-end training data; nothing is known between the evaluation points; the matte-collapse guard could not be checked with the available data.

auto_extend.title: Auto-extend
auto_extend.summary: Auto-extend only checks whether the keyframe fit is still improving and almost always continues; it cannot detect cases where longer training hurts the unseen frames (degrain).
auto_extend.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Useful for tasks that still gain from longer training, for example keying and clean-up (see [[ev:epochs]]).
- Not for degrain.

## Test conditions

Criterion: stop when a round of extension improves the keyframe accuracy by less than 0.20 dB. Replayed on the 27 cases of the main test set that have a longer comparison run (30k → 100k, 100k → 300k, same setting).

## Results

| Criterion | Cases | Decided to continue | Longer training better on unseen frames | Longer training worse on unseen frames |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stop when a round gains less than 0.20 dB | 27 | 27 | 18 | 9 (all degrain) |

- Criterion not used (measured): no extension once the keyframe PSNR exceeds 41 / 56 dB — right in 9 of the 27 cases and wrong in 18, 12 of which stopped clean-up runs whose unseen frames were still improving by 0.3–4.8 dB.
- When enabled, a run usually extends to the limit (at most 4 rounds of about 30% of the Epochs each, no more than 2.5 times the length).

## Limitations

Only the criterion was replayed, there is no end-to-end extension data; the learning-rate curve of the extension was not tested separately.

lab_stop_after_best.title: Stop after the best score
lab_stop_after_best.summary: The live score used by stop-after-best looks only at the training keyframes; in the test records the best score was almost always the final step, and in single cases training would stop too early.
lab_stop_after_best.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- Useful to save GPU time in batches of comparison runs.
- The score reflects only the fit of the training keyframes (plus a stability term for the unedited area), not the in-between frames.

## Test conditions

The live score was replayed on the records of the main test set (5 evaluation points per run), including runs of 300k Epochs and with the 2 px grid.

## Results

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Runs whose best score is at the final step (%) | about 99 |
| Best score before the final step, unseen frames better than at the final step | 3 (degrain on the 4 px grid, +0.16 to +0.27 dB) |
| Best score before the final step, unseen frames worse than at the final step | 1 (keying, 2 px grid, −0.90 dB) |

- In the last case the display PSNR of the training frames fell by 0.28 dB at the last evaluation point while the unseen frames were still improving.
- Rule not used (measured): treating a keyframe PSNR above 46 / 58 dB as saturated locks the final step in only 70.2% of the runs, unseen frames 0.48 dB lower on average over all runs.

## Limitations

There is no data on whether training would stop too early between the evaluation points.

preset_cleanup_grain.title: Preset: Clean-up
preset_cleanup_grain.summary: Clean-up preset = Medium + 1 px grid + gradient 0.05 + averaged weights. On Small these advanced parameters are 4.27 dB above the Nuke defaults (5.57 dB at 300k Epochs); Medium adds another 0.67 dB.
preset_cleanup_grain.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- For removing decals, tracking markers, stains and similar local edits from a few keyframes.
- For face retouching use [[ev:preset_face_edit]].

## Test conditions

Tracking marker / stain removal dataset ([[ev:appendix_material]]), Small and Medium, 5 keyframes, 3 seeds. Averaged weights were off during the measurement; they do not change the result at the final step ([[ev:adv_ema]]).

## Results

| Setting | Epochs | Unseen-frame PSNR (dB) | Δ relative to the Nuke defaults (Small, dB) | Display PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medium, 1 px + gradient 0.05 (preset) | 100k | 56.74 ± 0.31 | — | 56.33 |
| Small, 1 px + gradient 0.05 | 100k | 56.07 ± 0.13 | +4.27 | 55.89 |
| Small, 1 px + gradient 0.05 | 300k | 57.70 ± 0.14 | +5.57 | — |
| Small, plus Charbonnier 0.25, highlight damping 0.5, horizontal flip 0.5 (not included) | 100k | 54.19 ± 0.29 | +2.39 | 54.32 |

- The 1 px grid is the main source ([[ev:adv_crop_grid]]); gradient 0.05 mainly raises the display PSNR ([[ev:adv_loss_grad]]); averaged weights make mid-run checkpoints steadier ([[ev:adv_ema]]).
- Model Size: the full set of settings is 0.67 dB higher on Medium than on Small, higher for all 3 seeds, and 0.44 dB higher in display PSNR, at about 1.5 times the training time ([[ev:model_size]]). The preset uses Medium, the Nuke default. On Medium, gradient 0.05 again mainly raises the display PSNR (54.60 dB with 1 px alone).
- Charbonnier, highlight damping and horizontal flip brought no gain on this dataset ([[ev:adv_loss_charbonnier]], [[ev:adv_loss_hdr]], [[ev:adv_augment_flip]]).

## Limitations

One synthetic removal shot (960×540); face retouching and grainy live-action footage are not part of this test. The three Medium runs and the three Small runs were made on different machines (same data and scoring; for the differences between machines see repeatability in [[ev:method]]).

preset_keying_despill.title: Preset: Keying
preset_keying_despill.summary: Keying preset = Small + RGB→RGBA + 1 px grid + gradient 0.15 + averaged weights; on the tested green-screen dataset it is 4.59 dB above the Nuke defaults and the alpha SAD drops by about a third.
preset_keying_despill.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- For green-screen keys that output despilled premultiplied RGB and alpha together (3→4).
- The more keyframes, the better ([[ev:dataset_keyframes]]).

## Test conditions

Green-screen keying dataset ([[ev:appendix_material]]), Small, 5 keyframes, 3 seeds. Averaged weights were off during the measurement.

## Results

| Setting | Epochs | Unseen-frame PSNR (dB) | Δ relative to the Nuke defaults of the same length (dB) | Display PSNR (dB) | Alpha SAD (thousands of pixels) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nuke defaults | 100k | — | — | 46.87 | 0.22 |
| 1 px + gradient 0.15 | 100k | 63.58 ± 0.37 | +4.59 | 55.93 | 0.14 |
| 1 px + gradient 0.15 | 300k | 65.65 ± 0.32 | +3.97 | — | 0.098 |
| 1 px + Charbonnier 0.30 + gradient 0.15 + highlight damping 0.35 (not included) | 100k | 60.45 ± 0.19 | +1.46 | 52.93 | 0.17 |

- At 300k Epochs the alpha SAD of the Nuke defaults is 0.151.
- PSNR of the premultiplied RGB: Nuke defaults 63.1 dB, preset 70.5 dB.
- Components: 1 px grid ([[ev:adv_crop_grid]]), gradient 0.15 ([[ev:adv_loss_grad]]), averaged weights ([[ev:adv_ema]]). Charbonnier lowers the linear PSNR on keying ([[ev:adv_loss_charbonnier]]).
- Model size: Medium makes no difference ([[ev:model_size]]).

## Limitations

One green-screen shot with a ground truth from an analytic keyer; Large was not tested.

preset_bokeh_focus.title: Preset: Defocus
preset_bokeh_focus.summary: Defocus preset = Large + 1 px grid + Charbonnier 0.25 / gradient 0.10 / highlight damping 0.5 + stage ratios 15 / 25 / 60; on the tested defocus dataset it is 3.47 dB above the Nuke defaults at the same Large size.
preset_bokeh_focus.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- For bringing out-of-focus shots back into focus.
- There is no usable test data for motion blur.

## Test conditions

Defocus dataset ([[ev:appendix_material]]), 5 keyframes, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds; baseline: phase-aligned Nuke defaults.

## Results

| Setting | Model | Unseen-frame PSNR (dB) | Δ relative to the Nuke defaults of the same model (dB) | Display PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nuke defaults (phase-aligned) | Large | 39.20 ± 0.49 | — | 37.93 |
| Defocus preset | Large | 42.67 ± 0.41 | +3.47 | 40.98 |
| Preset without the three loss terms | Large | 42.37 ± 0.08 | +3.17 | 40.13 |
| Defocus preset | Small | 38.25 ± 0.23 | +1.95 | 37.11 |
| Preset without the three loss terms | Small | 38.20 ± 0.30 | +1.91 | 36.35 |

- The three loss terms make no difference in linear PSNR (Large −0.30, Small −0.05 dB) but do in display PSNR (Large −0.85, Small −0.77 dB; on Large all 3 seeds are below all seeds of the preset), at the same speed, so they stay in the preset.
- Components: 1 px grid ([[ev:adv_crop_grid]]), stage ratios ([[ev:adv_stages]]), Large ([[ev:model_size]]), Charbonnier ([[ev:adv_loss_charbonnier]]).

## Limitations

One synthetic disc-defocus shot; the three loss terms were not separated one by one on Large.

preset_degrain_clean.title: Preset: Degrain
preset_degrain_clean.summary: Degrain preset = Small + 1 px grid; loss terms have no effect on degrain, and neither larger models nor longer training help.
preset_degrain_clean.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- For removing grain and noise.
- About 100k Epochs of training is enough ([[ev:epochs]]).

## Test conditions

Degrain dataset ([[ev:appendix_material]]), Small, 5 keyframes, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds.

## Results

| Setting | Δ PSNR relative to 1 px alone (dB) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Plus Charbonnier 0.25 + gradient 0.05 + highlight damping 0.5 (not included) | +0.06 | no difference |
| Without 1 px, the three loss terms only | −0.82 | lower |

- The preset result is the result of 1 px alone, see the degrain row in [[ev:adv_crop_grid]].
- Model size: Small is best ([[ev:model_size]]); training length: no gain after 100k ([[ev:epochs]]).

## Limitations

One synthetic grain shot.

preset_roto_matte.title: Preset: Roto
preset_roto_matte.summary: Roto preset = Small + RGB→Alpha + 1 px grid; no advanced setting brought a measurable gain on roto, the result depends mainly on the density of the keyframes.
preset_roto_matte.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- For single-channel mattes from RGB footage.
- The main way to improve quality is more keyframes ([[ev:dataset_keyframes]]).

## Test conditions

Two roto datasets ([[ev:appendix_material]]), Small, 5 keyframes, 100k Epochs, 3 seeds.

## Results

| Setting | Parkour: Δ PSNR (dB) | Parkour: IoU | Dance: Δ PSNR (dB) | Dance: IoU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 px + Charbonnier 0.25 + gradient 0.05 (not included) | +0.22 | 0.865 | −0.33 | 0.687 |

- The 1 px grid makes no difference on roto ([[ev:adv_crop_grid]]) and is kept for consistency with the other presets; larger models are worse ([[ev:model_size]]).

## Limitations

2 shots; the dance shot has large pose changes, frames far from the keyframes lose quality clearly.

preset_face_edit.title: Preset: Face edit
preset_face_edit.summary: Face edit preset = Medium + RGB→RGB + 1 px grid + Charbonnier 0.25 + keyframe commonality + averaged weights. Keyframe commonality targets the inconsistency between hand-painted keyframes; on the public face test shots Medium is 0.87–2.62 dB above Small, and the 1 px grid and averaged weights point the same positive way. With Charbonnier 0.25, unseen-frame PSNR is 0.55 dB higher on average with consistent keyframes (every pair higher), and the changes in the unedited area drop under every keyframe condition (×0.23 – ×0.85).
preset_face_edit.body:
## Where it helps and where it does not

- For face shots where only some frames were painted by hand: wounds, blemish removal, beauty work, ageing / de-ageing, face-swap touch-up.
- Requirements: RGB→RGB, a dataset with a validation sequence, at least 3 keyframes (the conditions of keyframe commonality).

## Test conditions

Public face test shots ([[ev:appendix_material]]), Small, 100k steps, L1 loss, training seed 1; consistent keyframes.

Charbonnier 0.25: 5 public face shots (Wound paste A / B, Face ageing B, Skin retouch A, Wound removal A, [[ev:appendix_material]]) with the training settings of the preset: Medium, 1 px grid, averaged weights (β 0.9995), 100k Epochs, 5 keyframes (42 / 95 unseen frames), 3 seeds; the preset against "preset + Charbonnier 0.25" (gradient term and highlight damping 0), scored on the averaged weights (what is exported) against the consistent truth. Four keyframe conditions: identical to the truth, keyframe commonality off or on; 4 of the 5 keyframes with one local error each (painted weaker, stronger, 5–9 px off or with redrawn texture; simulated), keyframe commonality on; every keyframe a different version plus local errors (a simulated stress test: these keyframes are almost as far from the truth as the plate itself), keyframe commonality on. With keyframe commonality on, the keyframes first go through the product's keyframe commonality. Both runs of a pair ran on the same GPU model with the same torch version.

## Results

1 px relative to the 4 px grid:

| Shot | 1 px (dB) | 4 px (dB, mean of 3 seeds) | Δ (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Face ageing A (6 keyframes) | 50.29 | 49.98 | +0.31 |
| Face ageing B (11 keyframes) | 51.93 | 51.83 | +0.10 |
| Wound paste B (11 keyframes) | 52.67 | 52.23 | +0.44 |

- The 3 shots agree in direction but all stay below the 0.5 dB threshold.

Medium relative to Small:

## Limitations

The edits of the public face shots are synthetic (ageing, wound paste), with keyframes that agree or are made inconsistent by simulation; live-action shots with keyframes painted by an artist are not part of this test.
